text: A is the starting-point of the world of sound: even so is the Great Original the starting-point of all that exists.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail is all thy learning if thou worship not the holy feet of Him of the perfect intelligence ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whoso taketh refuge in the sacred feet of Him whose walk is among flowers, his days will be many upon the earth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who cleave unto the feet of Him who is beyond preference and beyond aversion: the ills of life touch them not ever.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who sing earnestly the praises of the Lord: they will be freed from the pain-engendering fruits of action both good and evil.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who follow the righteous ways of Him who hath burned away the desires of the five senses: their days will be many upon the earth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They alone escape from sorrow who take refuge in the feet of Him who hath no equal.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The stormy seas of wealth and sense delights cannot be traversed except by those who cling to the feet of the Sage who is the Ocean of Righteousness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Worthless indeed like the organs of sense which do not perceive is the head that boweth not at the feet of Him who is endowed with the eight attributes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They alone cross the ocean of births and deaths who take refuge in the feet of the Lord: the others traverse it not.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is by the unfailing fall of rain that the earth sustaineth itself: therefore is the rain called the immortal drink.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Every food that is sweet to the taste is given to man by Rain: and itself formeth also part of his food.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If rain should fail, famine would rage over the wide earth even though it is encircled by the ocean.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Husbandmen would cease to ply the plough if the fountains of the heavens are dried up.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is rain that ruineth, and it is rain again that setteth up those that it hath ruined.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even grass will cease to grow if the showers from above should cease to fall.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even the mighty ocean would reek with corruption if the heavens should cease to suck its waters and render them back to it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Sacrifices will not be offered to the Gods nor Feasts be celebrated on earth if the heavens are dried up.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Neither charity nor austerities will abide on the wide earth if the heavens should hold back their showers.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Nothing on earth can go on without water : so even right conduct itself depends ultimately on rain.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who have renounced sense-enjoyments and live a life of discipline: the scriptures exalt their glory above every other good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou canst not measure the greatness of ascetics: thou canst as well count the number of the dead.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who have weighed this life with the next and have renounced: the earth is made radiant by their greatness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man whose firm will controlleth his five senses even as the goad-ing hook controlleth the elephant: he is a seed fit for the fields of heaven.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The King of the Gods himself, Indra, is witness unto the might of him that hath burned away the five desires.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The great ones are they who can achieve the impossible: the feeble ones are those who cannot.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who appreciateth at their true value the sensations of touch and taste and sight and sound and smell he will command the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The scriptures of the world proclaim the greatness of the men of the mighty word.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is impossible to support even for a second the wrath of those who stand on the rock of renunciation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is saintly men that are to be called Brahmans: for it is they that have compassion on all life.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Righteousness leadeth unto heaven and it bringeth wealth also: what is there that is more profitable than Righteousness ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is no greater good than Righteousness, nor no greater ill than the forgetting of it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Be thou unremitting in the doing of good deeds: do them with all thy might and by every means.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Be pure in heart : all righteousness is contained in this one commandment: all other things are nought but empty sound.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Avoid envy and greed, anger and harsh words : that is the way to acquire righteousness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Say not in thy heart, I shall be righteous by and bye, but begin to do good works without delaying: for it is Righteousness will be thy undying companion on the day of thy death.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Ask me not, Where is the good of Righteousness? Look at the bearer of the palanquin and him that rideth on it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou do good all thy life without a single waste day, thou wallest up the road to future births.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That alone is delight which cometh of Righteousness: all else is pain and shame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That action alone is worth doing which is righteous: and all action must be shunned which is unrighteous.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The householder is the mainstay of all who follow the three other paths of life.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The householder is the friend of the orphan and the pauper and the helpless dead.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Five are the duties of the householder, namely, the offering of oblations to the dead, the performance of sacrifices to the Gods, the doing of hospitality, the rendering of help unto relations, and the looking after of one’s own self.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who feareth to do ill and doth charity before eating his meal : his seed decayeth never.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If love aboundeth in the home and righteousness doth prevail, the home is perfect and its end is all fulfilled.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man fulfilleth aright the duties of the householder, where is the need for him to take up other duties ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Among those that seek after salvation the greatest are they who lead a virtuous family life.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the householder who helpeth others in the observance of their vows and who leadeth a virtuous life himself : he is holier than the austere ones themselves.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Righteousness belongeth especially to the married life: and a good name is its ornament.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The householder who liveth as he ought to live will be looked upon as a God among men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: She is the good helpmate who possesseth every wifely virtue and spendeth not above her husband’s means.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: All other blessings turn to nought if the wife faileth in wifely virtues.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where is indigence if the wife is worthy ? and where is riches if worth is not in her ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is there that is grander than woman, when she is strong in the strength of her chastity ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the woman who worshippeth not other Gods but worshippeth her husband even as she riseth from bed : the rain-cloud obeyeth her commands.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: She is the good housewife who guardeth her virtue and her reputation, and tendeth her husband with loving care.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail is close confinement? It is her own continence that is the best guardian of a woman’s virtue.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the woman who hath begotten a worthy son: her place is high in the world of the Gods.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man whose home beareth not an honourable reputation: the proud lion-like walk in the sight of detractors is denied him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The chiefest blessing is an honourable home : and its crowning glory is worthy offspring.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: We know of no blessing so great as the begetting of children that are endowed with understanding.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man whose children bear an unstained character: no evil will touch him in any of his seven reincarnations.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Children are the veritable riches of a man: for they pass to him by their own acts all the merits that they acquire.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Sweeter verily than ambrosia is the plain soup bespattered by the tender hands of one’s own children.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The touch of children is the delight of the body: the delight of the ear is the hearing of their speech.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The flute is sweet and the guitar dulcet : so say they who have not heard the babbling speech of their little ones.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is the duty of the father to his son? It is to make him worthy to sit in the front rank in the assembly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To find oneself eclipsed in intelligence by one’s children is a delight to all the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Great is the joy of the mother when a male child is born unto her: but greater far is her delight when she heareth him called worthy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is the duty of the son to his father ? It is to make the world ask, For what austerities of his hath he been blessed with such a son ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where is the bar that can close in the gates of love ? The gentle tear-drops of lovers’ eyes are sure to proclaim its presence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that love not live only for themselves : as to those that love, their very bones are for others' occasions.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They say it is to taste again of love that the soul hath consented once more to be encased in bone.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Love maketh the heart tender towards all: and tenderness yieldeth that priceless treasure called friendship.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The blessing of the blessed, they say, is only the reward of a constant love.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They are fools who say that love is for the righteous alone: for even against the evil-minded love is the only ally for a man.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold how the sun burneth the boneless worm : even so doth Righteousness burn the man that doth not love.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that loveth not: he will know prosperity only when the sapless tree of the desert putteth forth leaves.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail is a lovely outside, if love, the soul’s ornament, hath no place in the heart ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The seat of life is in Love: who hath it not is only a mass of skin-encased bone.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What for do the wise toil and set up homes ? It is to feed the guest and help the pilgrim.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Were it even the draught of immortality, it shall not be tasted alone when the guest is in the hall.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: No evil befalleth the man who never faileth to honour the incoming guest.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who receiveth the worthy guest with his best smile: Lakshmi delighteth to abide in his home.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who feedeth his guest first and then only eateth what is left: standeth his land in need even of sowing?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath tended the out-going guest and waiteth for the incoming one: he is a welcome guest unto the Gods.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: We cannot say of any hospitable act by itself, So much is the merit of this act: it is the worth of the guest that is the measure of the sacrifice.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who performeth not the sacrifice of hospitality : he will say one day, I have toiled hard and laid me up a great treasure: but it is all in vain, for there is none to comfort me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Not to honour the pilgrim is veritable indigence in the midst of wealth: such a thing is found only with fools.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The anitcha flower fadeth by smelling : but a look is enough to break the heart of the guest.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The speech that is truly kind is the speech of the righteous men which is full of tenderness and free from dissimulation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Better even than a generous gift is sweet speech and a kind and gracious look.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the sweet and gracious look and the kind speech that cometh from the heart: Righteousness hath its dwelling place there.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who always speaketh words which gladden all hearts: Poverty, the increaser of sorrow, will never come to him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Modesty anda loving speech, these alone are the ornaments of man and none other.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Sinfulness will wane away and righteousness will increase if thy thoughts are good and thy speech is kind.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The word that is serviceable and kind createth friends and bringeth forth benefits.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Words that are kind and are removed from all littleness yield good in this life and in the next also.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Why doth not a man cease from violent words, even after he hath felt the sweetness that kind words give ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who useth hard words when sweet ones serve : he preferreth the unripe fruit to the ripe.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the kindness done without any obligation: even the heavens and the earth are too poor to repay it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A kindness done in the hour of need may look small : but it outweigheth the whole world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the kindness done without thought of recompense: it is mightier than the ocean.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The benefit received may be small even like a millet seed: but in the eyes of the just its measure is that of a palmyra tree.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Gratitude is not limited by the assistance given: it is bounded only by the nobility of him that receiveth it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Disregard not the friendship of the holy ones: forsake not those that succoured thee in difficulty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He that hath relieved from affliction shall be remembered with gratitude in every birth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is ignoble to forget a kindness: but an ill turn received it is the part of nobility to forget at once.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The mortallest injury is forgiven the moment the mind recalleth a single kindness received from the injurer.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is redemption for men who are guilty of every other crime: but the ingrate wretch shall know of none.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The just and the fair that giveth each man his due whether he is friend or foe, that is the good: nought else.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prosperity of the just groweth not less: it endureth even unto their remotest posterity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though nought but profit come of it, touch not the wealth that cometh by deviating from the right.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The righteous and the unrighteous are known by their offspring.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Evil and good come unto all: but an upright heart is the glory of the wise.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When thy heart swerveth from the right and turneth unto evil, know that thy destruction is near at hand.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The world looketh not down on the poverty of the upright and virtuous man.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the weighing beam, for it is straight in itself and weigheth justly : the glory of the wise is to be like unto it and to incline neither to this side nor to that.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who swerveth not at all from the right in his own mind: the upright speech of his lips is a judgment.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the business man that looketh after the interests of others as his own : his business will expand.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Self-control leadeth unto heaven, but uncontrolled passion is the royal road to endless darkness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Guard thy self-control as a very treasure: life hath no richer wealth here below.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who controlleth his passions consciously and by the right way : wisdom and every other blessing will come unto him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath triumphed over his passions and who swerveth not from duty: his form is more imposing than a mountain.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Humility is beautiful in all men : but alone on the rich doth it shine in all its splendour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who can draw in into himself his five senses even as the tortoise doth its limbs: he hath laid up for himself a treasure for all his future births.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whatever else thou rein not in, rein in thy tongue: for an unbridled tongue leadeth unto grief.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If even one word of thine causeth pain to another, all thy virtue is lost.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The burn caused by fire healeth in its time: but the wound burned in by the tongue remaineth green for ever.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath learned wisdom and whose mind is tranquil and under perfect control: Righteousness pilgrimageth to his home in order to have a look at him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man whose conduct is pure is honoured by all: purity of conduct is therefore to be prized even above life.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Watch anxiously over thy conduct : for wheresoever thou mayest search thou canst not find a firmer ally than right conduct.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Good conduct bespeaketh an honourable family : but low conduct placeth a man amongst the ignoble.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even the Védas if forgotten can be learned again: but once fallen from virtuous conduct the Brahman is fallen from his place for ever.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Prosperity is not for the envious : even so dignity is not for men of ill conduct.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The firm-minded swerve not from virtuous conduct: for they know the evils brought on by such swerving.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man of right conduct is honoured among men: but ignominy alone is the portion of those who fall therefrom.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Good conduct soweth the seed of prosperity: but an evil course is the mother of endless ills.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Foul words can never fall from the lips of the well-bred even when off their guard.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Fools may be as instructed as thou pleasest : but they never learn to conform to the ways of the Righteous.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose eyes are turned towards righteousness and towards wealth: they commit not the folly of desiring another man’s wife.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Among those that have fallen from virtue there is no greater fool than he that standeth at his neighbour’s threshold.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily they are in the jaws of death who invade the home of an unsuspecting friend.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let a man be ever so great: what availeth it all if he committeth adultery without thinking ever so little of the shame that floweth therefrom ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hangeth on to his neighbour's wife because she is accessible: his name is sullied for ever.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The adulterer knoweth no respite from four things, hatred, sin, fear, and shame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He is the righteous householder who careth not for the charms of his neighbour’s wife.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the high-souled man that looketh not on another’s wife: he is more than righteous : he is saintly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Who on earth deserve all the good things of the world? It is they who clasp not the arms of her who belongeth to another.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though thou shouldst transgress and yield to every other sin, it were well for thee if thou desire not thy neighbour's wife.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The earth supporteth even those that dig into her: even so bear thou with those that traduce thee; for that is greatness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Forgive thou always the injuries that others may do thee: but if thou forget them, it were even better.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The most shameful poverty is the refusal of hospitality : and the greatest strength is to bear with the dullness of fools.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou want to be grand always, be forgiving unto all.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The wise respect not the men who retaliate an injury : but they are prized as gold who forgive their enemy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The joy of revenge lasteth but a day: but the glory of him who forgiveth endureth for ever.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Be the wrong suffered ever so great: the better part is not to take it to heart and to abstain from revenge.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Conquer by thy nobility those that in their pride have injured thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: More saintly than even those that have renounced are they that bear with the bitter tongue of their detractors.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that do penance by fasting are great: but they only come after those that forgive their calumniators.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Guard thyself from envious thoughts: for freedom from envy is a part of virtuous conduct.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: No blessing is so great as a nature that is free from all envy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is he that careth not for virtue or for wealth that envieth his neighbour's prosperity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The wise injure not others through envy: for they know the evils that result therefrom.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Envy itself is scourge enough for the envious man: for, even if his enemies spare him, his own envy will work his ruin.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that beareth not to see gifts made to another: his family will beg for very food and clothing and perish.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Lakshmi cannot bear with the envious: she will abandon them to the care of her elder sister and quit their side.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Caitiff Envy bringeth on indigence and leadeth up to the gates of hell.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The affluence of the envious and the misery of the generous-minded are alike matter for wonder.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Never hath envy led to prosperity : nor a liberal heart to a fall therefrom.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who leaveth the right way and coveteth another man’s wealth: his wickednesses will increase and his family will decline.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that turn away from evil: they covet not, neither do they yield to ignoble deeds.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that care for other joys: they are not greedy after little delights, nor do they yield unto iniquity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that have mastered their senses and enlarged their vision : they covet not saying, Lo, we are in want.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail is a mind that is subtle and comprehending, if it yieldeth unto greed and consenteth unto insensate deeds ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even he who hungereth after grace and walketh in the path shall perish if he hankereth after wealth and plotteth evil.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Covet not the wealth that greed gathereth : for its fruit is bitter in the day of enjoyment.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou desire that thy substance should not grow less, covet not the riches in thy neighbour's hands.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the wise man that understandeth justice and coveteth not: Lakshmi knoweth his worth and seeketh him in his home.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The greed that looketh not beyond engendereth destruction: but the greatness that sayeth, I desire not, triumpheth over all.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who doeth iniquity and who speaketh not so much as the name of righteousness : it is sweet even unto him if men say, Lo, here is one who backbiteth not.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is wrong to turn away from good and do evil: but it is far worse to smile before and vilify behind.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is worthier to die at once than live by lying and slander: for such a death bringeth with it the fruits of righteousness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Slander not a man behind his back even though he hath insulted thee to thy very face.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The lips may speak righteousness : but a slanderous tongue betrayeth the meanness of the heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou slander another, he will look into thy own transgressions and expose the worst of them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They that know not to speak sweet and to make friendships create discord and separate men who were friends.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that speak abroad the transgressions of their friends, how will they spare the transgressions of their enemies ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How doth the Earth suffer patiently the tread of the calumniator on her bosom? Is it that she looketh unto Righteousness to rid her of him ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man can scan his own faults as he doth those of his enemies, can evil ever come to him?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that angereth the public by the speaking of vain words: he will be despised of all men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Worse even than injuring one’s friends is the speaking of vain words before many.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He that multiplieth empty words declareth loud his want of worth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that speaketh vain words in an assembly: no profit will come unto him and all that is good will flee from his side.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even the worthy will lose honour and respect if they indulge in vain speaking.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Call not him man who loveth idle words: call him rather a chaff among men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let the wise, if they deem it meet, speak even hard words: but it is good for them to desist from profitless speech.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The wise whose thoughts are set on great questions utter not words that are profitless and vain.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They whose eyes are whole say not vain words even by oversight.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Speak thou the speech that bringeth forth profit: but speak not ever words that are profitless and vain.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The evil fear not the folly called sin : but the worthy flee from it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Evil bringeth forth evil: evil therefore shall be feared even more than fire.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The chiefest wisdom, they say, is to abstain from injury even to an enemy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let not a man compass another's ruin even by oversight: for Justice will compass the ruin of him that plotteth evil.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let not a man work evil saying, I am poor: for, if he do, he will sink into a lower destitution than before.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whoso desireth not to be saddened by ills, let him abstain from doing injury to others.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a way of escape from every other enemy: but ill deeds never die but pursue and destroy their author.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: As the shadow leaveth not a man but doggeth his steps wherever he goeth, even so do evil deeds pursue their author and work his destruction.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man love his own self, let him not incline toward evil in any degree.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Know that man to be secure from ills who leaveth not the straight path in order to commit wrong.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The gracious expect no return when they oblige: how ever can the world repay the rain-cloud ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The substance gathered in by the worthy by the labour of their hands is all for others’ use.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A better thing than a gracious complaisance cannot be had either here or in heaven.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He alone liveth who knoweth what is proper : he who knoweth not what is fitting shall be classed with the dead.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the village tank filled with water to its brim: like unto it is the prosperity of the wise man that loveth the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Like unto a fruit-tree in the middle of the village bearing fruit is riches in the hands of the man of heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Like unto a tree that yieldeth medicinal drugs and drieth not is riches in the hands of the generous man.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who know what is just and proper: they fail not to oblige others even when fallen on evil days.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The complaisant man thinketh himself poor only when he is impotent to oblige those who solicit his aid.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If ruin cometh as a result of complaisance, it is worth courting even by selling one’s own self into slavery.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Giving to the poor is alone charity : all other giving is of the nature of loan.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though it lead unto heaven, receiving is bad: and though heaven should be denied to the giver, giving alms is a virtue.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is only the high-born man that giveth without ever meanly saying, I have not.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The heart of the giver is not glad until he seeth the smile of content on the face of the suppliant.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The conquest of conquests to the conqueror over self is the conquest over hunger: but his conquest cometh only after the conquest of him who appeaseth that hunger.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To fill the gnawing hunger of the poor: that is the way that the wealthy man should lay up riches for himself.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The evil disease called hunger toucheth not the man that divideth his bread with others.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The hard of heart who perish their wealth by hoarding it, have not they ever tasted the delight of giving unto others?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bitterer verily than the beggar’s bread is the hoarded meal of the miser eating alone.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Nothing is bitterer than death: but even death is sweet when one hath not the power to do charity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Give to the poor and add glory unto thy name: there is no greater profit for man than this.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The one theme in the mouth of all that praise is the glory of those that give unto the poor.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Everything else dieth on earth: but the fame that hath no rival endureth for ever.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that hath won a lasting, world-wide fame: the Gods on high prefer him even before saints.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The ruin that addeth unto fame and the death that bringeth glory belong only to the great-souled.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If men must needs be born into the world, let them earn glory: as to those who earn it not, it were better for them not to have been born at all.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that are not free from blemish chafe not at themselves: why then are they wroth against their calumniators ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is a disgrace for all men if they earn not the memory called fame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the land weighed down beneath the tread of an inglorious people: its riches, even though renowned in the past, will wane away.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They alone live who live without blemish : and they alone die who have lived without glory.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The chiefest wealth is a heart that is rich in mercy : for material wealth is found even in the hands of vile men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Reason by the right method and take up Mercy: and if thou inquire of all religions also, thou shalt see that Mercy is the only salvation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They enter not into the dark and bitter world whose heart is joined unto mercy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The results of actions at which the soul trembleth pursue not him who is kind and merciful to all life.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Affliction is not for the merciful : the teeming air-encircled earth is a witness thereto.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that hath forsaken mercy and doth iniquity: though he must have suffered cruelly in past births for abandoning virtue, he hath forgotten the lesson, say the wise.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The other world is not for those that have not mercy, even as this world is not for them that are without riches.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The poor in substance may one day thrive and prosper: but they that lack pity are poor indeed and their day cometh never.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is as easy for the hard of heart to do deeds of righteousness as for the confused in mind to realise the Truth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When thou art tempted to oppress the weak, consider how it would be for thee to tremble before a stronger.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How can he feel pity, who eateth other flesh in order to fatten his own?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Riches are not for the thriftless: even so pity is not for those that eat meat.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The heart of the man that tasteth flesh turneth not towards good, even as the heart of him that is armed with steel.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The killing of animals is veritable hardness of heart: but the eating of their flesh is iniquity indeed.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: In non-eating of flesh is Life : if thou eat, the pit of hell will not open its mouth to let thee out.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the world desireth not meat for eating, there will be none to offer it for sale.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man can only realise to himself the agony and pain suffered by other living beings, he would not desire to eat flesh-meat.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who have escaped from the bonds of illusion and ignorance: they eat not the flesh from which life hath flown out.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To abstain from the killing and eating of living things is better than to perform a thousand sacrifices in the sacrificial fire.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who killeth not and abstaineth from flesh-meat: all the world joineth hands to do him reverence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Patient endurance of suffering and non-injuring of life, in these is contained the whole of tapas.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Austerities are for the austere of heart : it is profitless for others to take them up.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is it because there should be some people to tend and feed ascetics that all the rest have forgotten tapas ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou wouldst destroy thy foes and exalt those that love thee, know that such a power belongeth unto tapas.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Tapas fulfilleth all desires even in the very manner that is desired: therefore is it that men endeavour after tapas in this world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is the men that do tapas that look after their own interests : the rest are caught in the snares of desire and only do themselves harm.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fiercer the fire in which it is melted the more brilliant becometh the lustre of the gold: even so the severer the sufferings endured by the austere, the purer their nature shineth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath attained mastery over himself: all other men worship him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that have acquired power by austerities : they can succeed even in conquering death.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the needy are the many in the world, it is because those that do tapas are few, and those that do not, the larger number.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The five principles of his own body Smile within themselves when they see the imposture of the hypocrite.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail is an imposing presence when evil is in the heart and the heart is conscious thereof ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the ungodly man putting on the puissant look of the austere: he is like a cow that grazeth about wearing a tiger’s skin.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who taketh cover under a saintly garb and doth evil : he is like a fowler hiding in the bush and catching birds.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The hypocrite pretendeth unto sanctity and sayeth, I have vanquished my passions: but he will come to grief and cry, What have I done? and what have I done ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that hath not renounced in his heart, but walketh about like one that hath renounced, and cheateth men : there is none more hard of heart than he.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The kunri seed is fair on one side, but the other side of it is black : there are men who are like unto it : they are fair on the outside, but their inside is all black.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Many there be whose heart is impure but who bathe in holy streams and prowl about.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The arrow is straight and the lute hath a bend: judge thou therefore men by their acts and not by their appearance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Neither matted hair thou wantest nor shaven head, if thou abstain from that which the world contemneth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whoso wanteth not to be held in contempt, let him guard himself against every thought of fraud.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is a sin even to say in one’s heart, I shall cheat my neighbour of his substance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fortune that is built up by fraud may appear to thrive: but it is doomed for ever.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The thirst for plunder leadeth in its season to endless grief.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that coveteth other men’s substance and lieth in wait to catch them napping: he thinketh not of grace and love is far from his heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man who thirsteth after plunder cannot weigh things aright: nor can he walk in the way of righteousness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that hath weighed the things of this world and made his heart firm : he committeth not the folly of cheating his neighbour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: As Righteousness resideth in the heart of him who valueth things aright, even so Deceit hath its seat in the heart of the thief.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who meditateth on nothing but theft and plunder: he will leave the right path and perish.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He that deceiveth others is not master even of his own body: but the world of the Gods itself is a never-failing inheritance unto the men that are righteous.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is truthfulness? It is the speaking of that which is free from even the slightest taint of evil.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even falsehood is of the nature of truth if it bringeth forth unmixed good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bear not false witness against thy neighbour : for thy own conscience will burn thee when thou hast lied.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man whose heart is free from falsehood: he reigneth in the hearts of all.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man whose heart is fixed in truthfulness: he is greater than the austere and greater than he that distributeth alms.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is no greater renown for a man than the renown that he is a stranger unto falsehood: such a man obtaineth every blessing without mortifying the body.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man can live without ever uttering a falsehood, all other virtue is superfluous unto him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The cleanliness of the body belongeth unto water: but the purity of the heart is proved by truthfulness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The worthy regard not all other light as light: it is only the light of truth that they look upon as a veritable illumination.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Many things have I seen in this world: but of all the things that I have seen, there is nothing that is higher than truth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He alone can be said to forbear who hath the power to strike: as to him that hath not the power, what mattereth it whether he forbeareth or forbeareth not?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is wrong to get angry even when thou art helpless to strike: and when thou hast the power, there is nothing that is worse than anger.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whoever thy offender may be, forget thy anger: for from anger springeth a multitude of ills.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Anger killeth the smile and it destroyeth cheer : hath mana crueller foe than anger ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou want to look after thyself, keep off from choler: for if thou keep not off, it will come upon thee and destroy thy own self.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Choler destroyeth every man whom it approacheth : and it burneth also the family of him who nurseth it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He who nurseth his rage as if it were a precious thing is like unto the man who dasheth his hand against the ground: the hand of this man escapeth not from injury, and the destruction of the first is as certain.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even when thy wrongs burn as the flaming of many fires, it is good if thou canst abstain from anger.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: All the desires of a man will be fulfilled on the instant if from his heart he banish anger.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whoso is overwhelmed with anger is like one dead: but whoso hath forsworn wrathfulness is like unto the saints.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The pure in heart injure not others even for the sake of the wealth that glorifieth a man: for that is their way.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even when another hath injured them in his hate, the pure in heart return not the injury : for that is their way.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou injure another, even though it be only a man who hath injured thee without any provocation, thou simply bringest down upon thyself evils that can never be remedied.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How shall a man punish them that have injured him? Let him do them a good turn and make them ashamed in their hearts.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail is intelligence to a man if he doth not look on others’ pain as his own and abstain from injuring any ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When a man hath felt a pain for himself, let him take care that he inflicteth it not on others.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is a great thing if thou injure not knowingly any man, at any time, and in any degree.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He who hath felt what pain meaneth to himself, how doth he bring himself to inflict it on others ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man injureth his neighbour in the forenoon, evil will come to him in the afternoon of its own accord.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: All evil recoileth on the head of the wrong-doer : they abstain therefore from wrong-doing who desire to be immune from ills.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The greatest of virtues is non-killing: killing bringeth in its train every other sin.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To divide one’s bread with the needy and to abstain from killing: this is the greatest of all the commandments of all the prophets.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The greatest virtue of all is non-killing : truthfulness cometh only next.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is the good way? It is the path that taketh thought how it may save even the smallest of creatures from being killed.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Among all that have renounced this life with its fears of ill, the chiefest is he that reverenceth all life for fear of killing any.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath taken the vow of non-killing : Death that eateth away all life maketh no inroads into his days.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Take not away from any living thing the life that is sweet unto all, even if it be to save thine own.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They may say, Sacrifices gain for a man many blessings: but to the pure in heart the blessings that are earned by killing are an abomination.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those who live by slaying are likened by the discriminating to eaters of carrion.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man whose putrid body is festering with ulcerous sores: he must have been a shedder of blood in the past, say the wise.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is no greater folly than the infatuation that looketh upon the transient as if it were everlasting.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The crowd that assembleth to witness a village show, that is the symbol of great riches flowing on a man: and the dispersal of that same crowd is the type of its passing away.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Prosperity is transient : if thou have come by it, delay not to do things that are of lasting good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Time looketh like an innocent thing : but verily it is a saw that is continually sawing away the life of man.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Make haste to do good works before the tongue is paralysed and hiccough ariseth in the throat.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: But yesterday a man was and to-day he is not: that is the wonder of wonders in this world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Man knoweth not if he shall last the next minute: but his thoughts are more than ten million.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fledgeling abandoneth the broken shell of the egg and flieth away : that is the symbol of the love between the soul and the body.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Death is like unto asleep: and life is like the waking after that sleep.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Hath the soul no home of its own, that it taketh shelter in this worthless body ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whatsoever thing a man hath renounced, from the grief arising from that thing hath he liberated himself.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou want joy, renounce early : for many are the delights that thou shalt enjoy after renouncing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Crush thou the five senses: and everything in which thou takest delight, give up utterly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To possess nothing, that is the law of the man of vows : the possession of even one thing is a coming back to the snares that he hath left.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To those that desire to put an end to their reincarnations, even the body is a superfluity : how much more then are other bonds?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The feelings of I and Mine are nought but vanity and pride: he who crusheth them entereth a higher world than the world of the Gods.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who holdeth on to attachments and giveth not them up: Grief shall take hold of him and shall not give him up.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They that have renounced utterly are on the path to salvation: but the others are caught in a snare.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The moment that attachments are broken, that very moment reincarnations cease: the man who breaketh them not continueth in vanity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Take thou refuge in Him who hath conquered all attachments: and hold fast to that ark in order that all thy bonds may be broken.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: From the delusion of taking vanities for the Reality a man cometh by a life of sorrow.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who is freed from delusion and who hath an unclouded vision : darkness ceaseth for him and joy cometh unto him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath freed himself from uncertainties and who hath realised the Truth: heaven is nearer to him than the earth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though risen to human birth, nought is gained if the soul realiseth not the Truth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To separate the true from the false in everything, whatever its nature may be, that is the part of a wise understanding.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath studied deeply and hath realised the Truth: he shall enter the path that leadeth not again into this world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily those that have meditated upon and attained to the Truth need not think at all of future incarnations.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is the part of Wisdom to desire to escape the folly called birth, and to aim at realising the Supreme and the Good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who understandeth the means of his salvation and laboureth to conquer all attachments : the ills that he is yet to suffer depart from him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: As desire and anger and delusion leave a man, his ills also follow their pace and slowly melt away.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Desire is the seed that yieldeth unto every soul, and always, a never-failing crop of births.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou must needs long for anything, long for freedom from reincarnation : and that freedom shall come to thee if thou long to conquer longing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is no greater wealth here below than desirelessness : and wherever thou goest thou canst find no treasure that equalleth it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Purity is nought but freedom from desire : and this freedom is achieved by yearning for perfect truthfulness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is those that have conquered their desire that are called the liberated ones: the others appear to be free but they are verily in bondage.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou love righteousness, flee from desire : for desire is a snare and a dis appointment.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man cutteth off utterly all his desires, salvation shall come to him by any path that he commandeth to it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He that hath no desires hath no grief: but ills on ills descend on the man that hankereth after things.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even here a man shall have everlasting joy if he killeth that greatest misery of all, desire.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Desire is never filled : but if a man giveth it up he attaineth perfection even at that very moment.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Resolution cometh to a man when Fortune is about to smile on him : but Indolence appeareth when Fortune is about to leave.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Evil fate dulleth the faculties: but when Fortune is about to smile she first expandeth the intelligence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What doth learning avail and all subtleties ? It is the Spirit that is inside that prevaileth over all.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There are two things in the world which have nothing in common : Riches is one thing and Saintliness is quite another.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When the tide is against thee even good things turn to evil: and even evil things turn to good when the tide is on.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What Destiny denieth thou canst not keep even with the utmost care: and even if thou scatter abroad, the things that are thine will not go away from thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even the man who hath amassed ten million cannot enjoy his riches except as the Ordainer hath ordained.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily the destitute poor would turn their hearts towards renunciation but that Destiny reserveth them for the miseries that are their portion.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He that rejoiceth when good cometh, why should he fret when he receiveth evil ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is there that is mightier than Destiny ? For even as its victim is meditating a plan to overcome it, it forestalleth him and bringeth him down.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He is a lion among princes who is well endowed in respect of the six things: troops, population, substance, council, alliances, and fortifications.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Four qualities should never be wanting in the prince, namely, courage, liberality, wisdom, and energy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that are destined to rule the earth: the three virtues, alertness, learning, and decision, leave them not.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prince shall not fail in virtue and shall abolish unrighteousness: he shall guard his honour jealously but shall not sin against the laws of valour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prince shall know how to develop the resources of his kingdom and how to enrich his treasury: how to preserve his wealth and how to spend it worthily.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the prince is accessible to all his subjects and is never harsh of word, his kingdom will be esteemed above every other.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who can give with grace and rule with love : his name will fill the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who administereth impartial justice and protecteth his subjects: he shall be called a God among men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who hath the virtue to bear with words that are bitter to the ear: the world will rest permanently under his umbrella.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who is liberal and gracious and just, and who tendeth his people with care: he is a light among kings.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Acquire thoroughly the knowledge that is worth acquiring: and after acquiring it walk thou in accordance therewith.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Two are the eyes of living kind: the, one is called Numbers, and the other: Letters.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The learned alone can be said to possess eyes : the unlettered have but two sores in their head.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The scholar bringeth joy with him wherever he cometh: but when he departeth he leaveth regrets behind.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though thou hast to humble thyself before the teacher even as a beggar before a man of wealth thou yet acquirest learning: it is those that refuse to learn that are the lowest among men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Knowledge is like unto a sand-spring: the more thou diggest and drawest thereat, the more excellent is the flow thereof.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Everywhere is his home to the learned man, and everywhere his native land: why then doth a man neglect instruction up to his dying day ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The learning that a man hath acquired in one birth will exalt him even in all his succeeding incarnations.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The learned man seeth that the learning that delighteth him delighteth also all that listen to him: and he loveth instruction all the more on that account.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: An imperishable and flawless treasure is learning to a man: other wealth is as nothing before it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Ascending the rostrum without abundant knowledge is like the playing of dice without the chequered board.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man without learning who desireth to be called eloquent: he is like unto a woman without busts who yearneth to be admired of men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even a fool shall be counted wise if he can hold his peace before the learned.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The opinion of an ignorant man will be rejected by the wise even though it may be perfectly sensible.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the ignorant man who is wise in his own eyes: he will be put to shame directly he openeth his lips in an assembly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Like unto a waste land that yieldeth no harvests is the man that hath neglected instruction: all that men can say about him is that he liveth, and nothing more.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man whose understanding hath not been penetrated by the Grand and the Subtle : the comeliness of his person is no better than the beauty of an image of clay.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bitter verily is the poverty of the man of learning: but far worse is riches in the hands of the fool.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fool though born of a higher family is esteemed much less than a learned man who is of inferior descent.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How much better are men than beasts ? Even so much are the learned better than those that have not cared for instruction.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The most precious of treasures is the treasure of the ear: verily it is the crown of all kinds of wealth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even unto the stomach some food will be offered when there is no more food to be offered to the ear.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who have listened to much instruction: they are very Gods on earth.
