author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let a man hear instruction even though he hath no learning: for it will be a stay unto him when he is encompassed by difficulty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The counsel of the righteous is like unto a strong staff: for it keepeth those that listen to it from slipping.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Listen to good words though they be but few: even those few will add to thee a proportionate dignity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that hath meditated much in himself and hath laid by a store of instruction by listening to the wise: he talketh not nonsense even when in error.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Deaf indeed though it heareth is the ear that hath not been drilled by words of instruction.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Humility of speech is hard to be attained by those who have not listened to the subtle words of the wise.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that taste with the tongue but know not the taste of the ear: what doth it matter to the world whether they live or die?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The understanding is an armour against all surprise: it is a fortress which even enemies cannot storm.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is the understanding that curbeth the senses from roving about, keepeth them from evil, and directeth them towards the Good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To separate the true from the false in every utterance, whoever it be that speaketh, that is the part of a wise understanding.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What he speaketh, the wise man speaketh so as to be understood by all: and from the lips of others he gathereth their subtle meanings.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The wise man is sociable with all the world: and his temper is ever even, expanding not nor contracting to excess.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is a part of wisdom to conform to the ways of the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man of understanding knoweth what is coming: but the fool foreseeth not what is before.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is folly to rush headlong into danger : it is the part of the wise to fear what ought to be feared.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man of foresight who is armed for every contingency : he will never know the blow that causeth trembling.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He that hath understanding hath everything: but the fool though he possess everything hath nothing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who is free from haughtiness and anger and the vulgar passion : there is a dignity about him that adorneth his prosperity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Parsimony, over-confidence, and excessive amour propre are faults in the prince.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who are jealous of their reputation: though their fault be small even like a millet seed, they look upon it as of the measure of a palmyra tree.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Guard thyself jealously against weak-nesses : for they are the foes that will lead thee to ruin.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who provideth not beforehand against surprise: he will be destroyed even like a stack of straw before a spark of fire.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the prince correcteth his own faults and then looketh into those of others, where is the ill that can approach him ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the miser that spendeth not where he ought to spend: his wealth will come to an inglorious wreck.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Close-fisted parsimony is not a vice to be classed with other vices: it formeth a class apart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Exult not at anything at any time: embark not on enterprises that would bring thee no good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou canst keep from the knowledge of others the things in which thy heart taketh delight, the machinations of thy foes will be in vain.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Esteem thou the men that have grown old in righteousness, and acquire their friendship.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who can cure the evils that have already befallen thee and who can guard thee from future ones : cultivate thou their friendship with ardour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is the rarest of rare good fortunes if a man can secure to himself the devotion of men of worth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If those that are worthier than thyself have become thy intimates, thou hast acquired a strength before which all other strength paleth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: As the eyes of the prince are his own ministers, let him use his discretion and choose them wisely.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who can move with the worthy as their intimate: his foes will be powerless against him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Who can ruin the man that commandeth the friendship of those that can reprove him?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who reposeth not on the support of men who can rebuke him: he will perish even when he hath no foes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Profit is not for those that have no capital: even so stability is not for them that repose not on the firm support of the wise.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is foolish to make a multitude of foes: but it is ten times worse to give up the intimacy of the good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Men of worth fear vulgar company : but little-minded men mix with it as if they made one family with it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Water altereth and taketh the character of the soil through which it floweth : even so the mind taketh the colour of the company with which it con-sorteth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The understanding of a man belongeth unto his mind: but his reputation dependeth on the company he keepeth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The disposition of a man seemeth to reside in his mind: but its veritable abode is the company in which he moveth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Purity of heart and purity of action depend upon the purity of a man’s company.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The pure of heart shall have a righteous progeny: and everything prosper-eth unto those that consort with good company.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Purity of heart is a treasure unto a man: and virtuous company bringeth him every glory.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though themselves are endowed with every virtue, the wise look upon the company of the pure as a tower of strength.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Virtue leadeth unto heaven : and the company of the good steadieth a man in the practice thereof.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is no greater ally toa man than good company : and nothing injureth so much as evil company.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Take into thy consideration the output and the wastage and the profit that the undertaking will yield: and then put thy hand to it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who decideth upon action only after consulting with men chosen for their worth : there is nothing that is impossible for him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There are enterprises that tempt with a great profit but which perish even the capital itself: the wise undertake them not.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who fear to be ridiculed by others: they start not on any enterprise without previous deliberation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To make war without planning every detail of it beforehand is only to transplant thy enemy on carefully prepared soil.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There are things that ought not to be done and if thou do them thou wilt be ruined: and there are things that ought to be done and if thou do them not thou will be ruined also.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Decide not upon any action except after careful deliberation: it is a fool who undertaketh first and sayeth in his heart, I shall think afterwards.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that goeth not to his work the right way about: all his labour will be a waste even if numbers come to his aid.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even in doing good thou mayest err, if thou suit not the benefit to the character of him that receiveth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let the thing that thou decidest on be above reproach : for the world despiseth the man who stoopeth toa thing that is beneath himself.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Weigh justly the difficulty of the enterprise, thy own strength and the strength of thy enemy, and the strength also of your allies: and then enter thou upon it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who knoweth his own force and hath learned what he ought to learn, and who oversteppeth not the limits of his force and information : his invasions will never fail.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Many there have been who in the Sanguineness of their hearts over-estimated their strength and adventured, but were cut off in the middle.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who know not to live in peace, who know not their own measure and who are full of self-conceit : they will have a swift end.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Put too many of them and even peacock’s feathers would break the waggon’s axle.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that have climbed to the top of the tree will lose their lives if they attempt to climb still higher.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Keep thou in mind the extent of thy wealth and let thy gifts be commensurate therewith: that is the way to conserve and divide thy substance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It mattereth not if the feeder channel is strait, provided that the draining channel is not wider.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that taketh not account of his measure nor liveth within the bounds thereof: he may look like prospering, but he will perish leaving no trace behind.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that measureth not his wealth and lavisheth it with an unsparing hand : his substance will quickly come to nought.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The crow triumpheth over the owl when it is day: so opportunity is a great thing to the prince who would vanquish his enemy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To follow closely on the pace of Time : that is the cord that will bind Fortune to thee firmly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where is the thing called impossible if thou start on thy enterprise with a knowledge of the right season and employ the proper means ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou canst conquer even the whole world if thou choose the proper time and the proper objectives.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that are intent on conquests will be quietly watching their opportunity : they will know neither confusion nor hurry.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The ram steppeth back before it delivereth the crushing blow : even such is the inaction of the man of energy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The wise show not their anger on the spot : they will nurse it within their hearts and wait for their opportunity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bend down before thy adversaries . till the day of their decline : when that day is come thou mayest easily throw them down headlong.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When thou hast got an unusual chance, hesitate not but straightway attempt even the impossible.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When the time is against thee feign inaction like the stork: but when the tide is on, strike with the swiftness of its souse.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Provoke no war and begin no operation except after making a thorough reconnaissance of the theatre of opera-tions.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is an immense advantage even to the powerful and the strong to be based on fortified places.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even the weak can hold their own and triumph over a powerful foe if they choose the proper theatre and operate cautiously.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The plans of thy adversaries will be baffled if thou fall back on strong positions and base thyself on them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: All-powerful is the crocodile in deep water : but out of it, it is the plaything of its foes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The strong-wheeled chariot runneth not on the sea: nor saileth the ocean-going ship on dry land.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince that hath planned everything beforehand and striketh at the proper objective : he wanteth no other ally than his own valour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the prince whose army is weak only betaketh himself to a proper theatre of war, all the endeavours of his strong foe would be vain against him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if they have no proper defences . and other advantages it is hard to beat a people on their own soil.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the high-mettled elephant that hath faced without wincing a whole multitude of lancers: even a jackal will triumph over him when he is entangled in marshy ground.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Love of the right, gold, pleasure, and fear of life, these four are the tests of a man : give thy confidence therefore to men that satisfy all these tests.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who is born of a good family, who is free from faults and who dreadeth disgrace : he is the man for thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even men of rare learning and of pure hearts will not be found, when thou dost test them, to be absolutely exempt from all ignorance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Weigh a man’s good and weigh his evil : whichever is more, take that to be his nature.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Dost thou want to find out whether a manis noble or little-minded ? Know that conduct is the touchstone of character.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Beware of trusting men that have no kindred : for their hearts will be without attachment and they will be callous to shame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou choose a fool for thy confidential adviser because that thou lovest him, he will lead thee to endless follies.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that trusteth another without trying him: he createth endless evils even unto his posterity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Trust not a man without trying him : and after trying your men, give each of them the work for which he is fit.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To trust a man whom thou hast not tried and to suspect a man whom thou hast found worthy lead alike to endless ills.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that seeth the good and seeth the evil also and chooseth only that which is good: employ thou him in thy service.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that is able to develop the resources of thy kingdom and to cure the ills that may befall it : set him to manage thy affairs.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let him alone be selected for service who is endowed with kindness and intelligence and decision, and who is free from greed.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Many are the men that satisfy every test and yet alter in the actual performance of duty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Work should be entrusted to men in consideration of their expert knowledge and capacity for patient exertion, and not of their love towards thy person.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Choose the expert and give him the work for which he is fit: see that the time is ripe for performance and then get him to begin it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Determine first the capacity of the servant and the work for which he is fit: and then leave him in responsible charge of the same.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: After thou hast decided that a man is fit for an office, make him worthy to fill it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who resenteth the friendly advances of the servant who is skilful at his work: Fortune will depart from him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let the prince oversee everything every day: for there will be nothing wrong with the country so long as there is nothing wrong with the officers of the State.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Constancy of attachment even in adversity belongeth only unto kindred.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man is blessed with kindred whose love for him bateth not, his fortunes will never cease to grow.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man who rejoiceth not in the-intimacy of his kindred is like a tank without bunds : the waters of prosperity will flow away from him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To gather and attach one’s kindred to oneself: that is the use and purpose of prosperity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man have a sweet tongue and a liberal hand his kinsmen will gather round him in serried ranks.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that giveth freely and entertaineth not anger: the world hath none who hath a more attached kindred than he.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The crow concealeth not its food selfishly from its fellows but shareth it lovingly with them: prosperity will abide only with men of a like nature.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is good if the prince treateth not all his kinsmen alike but hath a graduated scale for each : for there are many that have an eye to privilege.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The estrangement of a kinsman is easily remedied: remove the cause of the coolness and he will come back to thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When a kinsman that hath broken with thee cometh back to thee for a reason, accept thou him, but with caution.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Worse than excessive rage is the unguardedness that cometh of self-complacency.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A false sense of security killeth glory even as indigence crusheth the under-. standing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Glory is not for the unwatchful: that is the conclusion of every school of thinkers in the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what use are fortresses to the cowardly ? or abundance of resources to the incautious ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He who faileth to guard against everything beforehand will deplore his negligence when he is surprised by disaster.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou relax not in thy vigilance at all times and against all men, there is nothing like it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Nothing is impossible to the man who can bring unto his work a mind that is ever wakeful and cautious.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prince shall devote himself assiduously to works that are commended by the wise: if he neglect them he will suffer in all his future births.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When thou art tempted to be self-complacent and elated, call to thy mind those that have perished by their supineness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily it is easy for a man to achieve all that he desireth, provided he keepeth his purpose constantly before his mind.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Deliberate well and lean not to either side : be impartial and consult with the men of law: that is the way to administer justice.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The world looketh up to the rain-cloud for life: even so do men look up to the sceptre of the prince for protection.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The sceptre of the prince is the mainstay of the science of the Brahmans and of righteousness also.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the noble prince who ruleth the people of his dominions with loving care : sovereignty will never depart from him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who wieldeth the Sceptre in accordance with the law: seasonal rains and rich harvests have their home in his land.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is not the lance that bringeth victory unto the prince: it is rather his sceptre, and that provided it is straight and leaneth not to either side.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prince is the protector of all his people : and him his sceptre shall guard, provided he alloweth it not ever to lean to either side.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who is not easy of access and who judgeth not causes with care: he will fall from his place and perish even when he hath no enemy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince that guardeth his subjects from enemies both within and without : if he punish them when they go wrong it is not a blemish : it is his duty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Punishing the wicked with death is like the removing of weeds from the corn-field.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who oppresseth his subjects and doth iniquity: he is worse than an assassin.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A request from him who holdeth the sceptre is like the stand and deliver of the highway robber.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who doth not oversee his administration every day and remove the irregularities therein : his sovereignty will wear away day by day.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the thoughtless prince whose rule swerveth from the ways of justice : he will lose his kingdom and his substance also.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily it is the tears of those groaning under oppression that wear away the prosperity of the prince.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is just rule that bringeth renown unto princes: and an unjust government darkeneth their glory.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How fareth the earth under a rainless sky ? even so fare the people under the rule of a cruel prince.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The condition of the rich man is more galling than that of the poor under the rule of the tyrant prince.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The heavens will not send showers in their season if the prince swerveth from justice and right.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The udders of the cow will be dried up and the Brâhman will forget his science if the prince ruleth not with justice.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prince shall measure the guilt of the offender and punish him so that he offend not again: but the punishment shall not be excessive.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that desire that their power shall last, let them brandish the rod smartly but lay it on soft.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who ruleth with a rod of iron and causeth anguish unto his people : he shall stand without a friend and perish forthwith.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince whose cruelty is a by-word among his people: his days will be shortened and he will perish forthwith.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the dour-faced prince who is inaccessible to his people: the wealth in his hands is like treasure guarded by a demon.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the prince is harsh of word and unforgiving, his prosperity, be it ever so great, will come to an end quickly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Words that are harsh and punish-ments that are excessive are the files that file away the iron of power.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who will not take counsel with his councillors but who falleth into a passion when his projects fail : his prosperity will wane away.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who looketh not to his defences while yet there is time: when he is surprised by a war he will be seized with trembling and perish quickly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The tyranny that yoketh to itself charlatans is the only burden under which the earth groaneth : there is none other beside.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold that ravishing Beauty called Considerateness: the world cannot go on smoothly without her.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Inconsiderateness have the amenities of life their existence : those who possess it not are a burden unto the earth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To what end is the song that cannot be sung? and what is the worth of the eye that showeth not indulgence ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is the use of eyes that merely show in the face, if they show not consideration for others according to their measure ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Indulgence is the ornament of the eye: the eye that hath it not will be looked upon as a mere sore.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose eyes show not consideration towards others: verily they are no better than the trees of the earth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily they are blind, those who are not considerate towards others : and there are none that truly see but are indulgent to others' faults.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who can be considerate towards others without derogating from any of his duties: he will inherit the earth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is nobility to forbear and show indulgence even unto those that have offended thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those who desire to be styled the very pink of courtesy will drink off even the poison that hath been mixed for them before their very eyes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let the prince understand that Political Science and his Intelligence Corps are the eyes wherewith he seeth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is the duty of the prince to learn betimes everything that befalleth every man and every day.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince that learneth not the happenings about him by means of scouts and spies : conquests are not for him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prince shall set spies to watch closely the officers of the realm, his own kindred, and his enemies.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who can wear an unsuspicious appearance, who will not know confusion before any man, and who can guard his secrets from ever leak-ing out : he is the proper man for the work of Intelligence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Spies and scouts shall disguise themselves as ascetics and holy men, and their investigation shall be thorough: and whatever is done them, they shall not let out their secrets.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who can draw out secrets from others and whose information is ever unconfused and clear : he is the man for the work of intelligence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even the information that hath been obtained by a spy shall be tested by that of another.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: See that no spy knoweth the others engaged in the same work : when three reports agree, thou mayest give credence to them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Reward not openly thy officers of Intelligence: for if thou do, thou merely lettest out thy own secret.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that possess energy are alone to be called rich : as to those that possess it not, do they really possess what they own?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Energy is the veritable possession of aman : for wealth endureth not for ever and will depart from him one day.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that hold in their hands the resource called energy : they will never despair, saying, Alas, we are ruined !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who remitteth not ever from his activity: Good Fortune Inquireth the way to his home.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The water with which a plant is watered is the measure of the luxuriance of its flower : even so, the spirit of a man is the measure of his fortunes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let all thy purposes be grand: for then even if they fail, their glory will tarnish never.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Men of spirit flinch not before a defeat: the elephant planteth his legs only more firmly when he is hit by the deep-piercing arrow.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that are wanting in energy: the glory of an exhaustless liberality can never be theirs.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What availeth his size and his sharp tapering tusks? The heart of the elephant sinketh when he seeth the tiger spring.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Exuberance of spirit, that alone is strength: those that have it not are mere stocks : their human bodies alone make the difference.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The perennial light called Family will be extinguished if it is invaded by the foul vapour of sloth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let them call sloth by its real name and avoid it, those who desire to establish their family on a solid foundation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the fool who huggeth assassin sloth unto his heart: his family will fall even before his day is ended.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who are sunk in sloth and who turn not their hand to any noble undertakings : their family will go to ruin and their vices will grow apace.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Procrastination, forgetfulness, sloth, and sleep, these four are the cosy pleasure boats of those that are fated to perish.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The slothful can never thrive in the world even though they have the favour of princes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who are slothful and who turn not their hand to any noble undertakings : they will listen to much reproof and contumely.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If sloth find a home in a family, the family will soon be in bondage to its foes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The afflictions that may have befallen a man’s family will cease to exist the moment he giveth up sloth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince that knoweth not sloth: he will bring within his sway all that hath been measured by the steps of Trivikrama.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Shrink not from any work saying, It is impossible : for labour will give thee the strength to achieve everything.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Beware of leaving any work unfinished : for the world careth not for those that do not complete the work that they have once begun.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The proud pleasure of being able to serve all men belongeth only to the greatness that shrinketh not from any exertion.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Like unto a sword in the hands of a eunuch is the liberality of the indolent man : it will not endure.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man who loveth not pleasure-but loveth work is a pillar of strength unto his friends and will wipe away: their tears of grief.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Industry is the mother of Prosperity: but Indolence only bringeth forth Misery.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: In sloth hath the Genius of Wretchedness her home: but the Lotus-born One resideth in the labour of him who yieldeth not to sloth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is no shame if fortune faileth a man : but it is a disgrace if he abstain deliberately from exertion.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even though the Gods be against, Industry is bound to pay the wages of labour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They will snap their fingers even at Destiny who succumb not to it but labour unremittingly in despite of it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When thou meetest with misfortune face it with thy best smile: for there is nothing like a smile to enable a man to hold his own against it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A whole sea of troubles will abase themselves the moment a shifty mind collecteth itself to face them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Troubles they send away troubled who trouble not themselves at the sight of troubles.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who is prepared to strain his every nerve like the bull-buffalo to wade through every difficulty : he may meet with obstacles but he will send them away disappointed.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man whose heart sinketh not even at a whole host of troubles arrayed against him: the obstacles in his path have themselves met with an obstacle.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The men that exult not at good fortune, can they ever fret themselves saying, Alas! we are ruined ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The wise know that the body is a target unto misfortune: and so they worry themselves not when they meet with a calamity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who loveth not pleasure and who knoweth that difficulties are a part of the law of things: he smarteth not ever under any check.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man who runneth not after pleasure in the day of success suffereth not pain in the day of failure.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who looketh upon the stress and strain of exertion as a veritable joy : he will be extolled by his very enemies.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who judgeth aright the ways and means of achieving great enterprises and the proper season to commence them : he is the proper man for the Council.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Study, resolution, manly exertion, and loving attention to the welfare of the people, these four make along with the last the five qualifications of the Councillor.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He is the able minister who possesseth the capacity to disunite allies, to cherish and keep up existing friendships, and to reunite those who have become enemies.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Judgment in the choice of projects and the means of their execution,, and positiveness in the expression of opinion are necessary qualities in the Councillor.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who knoweth the law and aboundeth in instruction, is deliberate in his speech and always understandeth what is fit for each occasion : he is the Councillor for thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is there that is too subtle for men who add knowledge of books unto natural intelligence ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even though thou art wise in thy knowledge of books, gather thou the wisdom of experience and act in accordance therewith.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prince may bea fool and may thwart him at every step: but the duty of the Councillor is always to point to him what is just and proper.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the minister that sitteth in the Council and plotteth the ruin of his prince: he is more dangerous than seven hundred million enemies.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The irresolute may even plan perfectly : but they will waver in the course of the execution and will never accomplish their designs.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The blessing of the tongue is a blessing indeed : for it is a blessing apart and formeth not part of other blessings.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: guard thou therefore against imprudence of speech.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the speech that bindeth friends more closely and fascinateth even enemies: that alone is worthy of its name.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Weigh each circumstance aright and then speak the speech that is fit : for the increase of righteousness and profit there is no other thing of more worth to thee than it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Speak thou the speech that cannot be silenced by any other speech.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To speak so as to captivate one’s own hearers and to seize the sense in the words of others, that is the part of the consum mate statesman.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who is eloquent of speech and knoweth neither confusion nor fear: it is impossible for any one to beat him in debate.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose speech is well ordered and couched in persuasive language : the world will be at their beck and call.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily they have a passion for much speaking who know not to say their mind in few and well chosen words.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who cannot expound unto others the knowledge that they have acquired: they are like unto the flower that blossometh but giveth forth no fragrance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Alliances bring success unto a man : but purity of action fulfilleth his every desire.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Always turn thy face away from those deeds that bring not glory as well as profit.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that desire to rise in the world, let them abjure all action that can tarnish their glory.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who see things in their right proportions: even when fallen on evil days they stoop not to action that is dishonourable and mean.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let not a man do those things which make him cry afterwards, what is it that I have done? and if he hath done any such thing, it is good for him if he doth it not once again.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let not a man do those things that good men condemn, even to save the mother that bore him from starvation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The indigence of the worthy is better far than wealth that is amassed by dishonourable means.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that shun not those things that are forbidden by good morals: they will come to grief even if they succeed in their designs.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: All that is wrong in the midst of tears will depart also accompanied by weepings: but that which is acquired by righteous ways, even if lost in the middle, increaseth in the latter end.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To try to lay by wealth by means of guile is like trying to preserve water in a pot of clay that is not baked.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Greatness of achievement is nought else but the greatness of the will that striveth therefor : all other things come not near the mark.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To avoid all action that is bound to fail and not to turn away from one’s purpose because of obstacles : these two are said to be the guiding principles of the wise.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man of action letteth his purpose appear only when that purpose Is achieved : for an untimely disclosure would create obstacles that cannot be surmounted.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To say a thing is easy for any man : but to do it in the manner undertaken is a rare thing indeed.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath acquired a name for the doing of great deeds : his services will be greatly in request with the prince and will be esteemed by all.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That which they will, men acquire even In the manner that they will, provided they will with all their might.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Despise not a man for his look: for there are men who are even as the axle-pin of the mighty rolling car.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When thou hast resolved upon a thing with all thy wits about thee, waver not but pursue thy purpose with vigour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Take up the doing of works that increase happiness: and even if thou have to suffer cruel mortification in the doing of them, steel thy heart and persevere to the end.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that have not the ambition to do great deeds: the world will not care for them whatever their other virtues may be.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The end of all deliberation is to arrive at a decision: and when a decision is come to, it is wrong to delay the execution thereof.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Do with deliberation those things that ought to be done in a leisurely way : but put not off even for a moment those things that require prompt action.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Go straight for the goal whenever circumstances permit: but when circumstances are against, follow along the path that offereth the least resistance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Uncompleted work and enemies that are left unsubdued are like unextinguished sparks of fire: they will grow betimes and overwhelm the perfunctory man.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Five things should be carefully considered in the doing of all action, namely, the resources in hand, the instrument, the nature of the action itself, the proper time and the proper place for its execution.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Determine first the exertion necessary, the obstacles in the way, and the expected profit, and then undertake thy enterprise.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The way to succeed in any undertaking is to learn the secret thereof from the man who is an expert in it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Men decoy one elephant by means of another : even so make one enterprise: the means of achieving a second.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Placate enemies even more swiftly than thou rewardest friends.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The weak should not care to live in the midst of constant alarms : when an opportunity offereth itself they should submit to an alliance with the strong.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A kind heart, high birth, and manners that captivate princes, these are the qualifications of the ambassador.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A loving nature, a wise understanding, and skill in speech, these three are indispensable to the envoy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who undertaketh to speak before princes words that shall profit his master: he shall be a scholar among scholars.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let that man go on embassies who possesseth intelligence and learning and a commanding presence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Conciseness of speech, sweetness of tongue and a careful eschewing of all disagreeable language, these are the means by which the ambassador shall work his master’s profit.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Learning, sangfroid, persuasive speech, anda just instinct for what is meet for each occasion, all these are necessary qualifications in the envoy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He is the fittest ambassador who hath a just eye for time and place, who knoweth his duty, and who weigheth his words before uttering them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man that is sent on embassies shall be firm of mind, pure of heart, and engaging in his ways.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the firm-minded man that will never let fall from his lips words that are weak and unbecoming : he is the fit man to deliver the messages of princes at foreign courts.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even when threatened with death the perfect ambassador will not fail in his duty but will endeavour to secure his master’s profit.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whoever desireth to move with princes, let him be like unto the men that warm themselves ata fire: let him not approach too near nor stand too far away.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Not to itch for those things that the prince desireth : that is the secret of acquiring his lasting favour and thereby growing in affluence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou desire not to fall into disgrace steer clear of all graver failings: for once suspicion is roused, it is impossible for any one to remove it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Speak not in whispers in the presence of the great ones : nor smile to another's face when they are near.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Do not try to overhear any conversation nor to fish out that which is withheld from thee: and then only receive the secret when it is imparted to thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Take into thy consideration the humour of the prince and the season that is, and then speak the words that will please him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Speak those things before the prince that are pleasant to him: but things that are unprofitable, speak not ever even if he demandeth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Trifle not with the prince because he is young or because he is thy kinsman or connection: but walk with awe before the light that is within him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose vision is unconfused and clear: they never do things that displease the prince, saying, we are favoured of him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: 'The men that rely on their intimacy with the prince and do unworthy deeds will perish.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who divineth what is in the mind before the voice uttereth it : he is an ornament unto all the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Look upon that man as a God who divineth with certitude that which is in the heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that can judge a man’s intentions from his looks: take them into thy council at whatever cost.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The men that understand without words may have the same features with the men that do not so understand: but they form a class apart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is the place of the eye among the organs of sense, if it divineth not by a look that which is in the heart?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as the crystal changeth and assumeth the colour of that which is near, even so doth the face alter and show that which overfloweth the heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is there that is subtler than the face ? for whether the heart is angry or glad it is the face that expresseth it first.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou canst find a man that is able to read the inside of thy heart without words, it is enough that thou merely lookest towards him and thy wishes will be fulfilled.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If there are men who understand its moods and tricks, the eye alone will declare whether there is hatred in the heart or friendship.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The measuring rod of those that call themselves subtle is, when thou search for it, nought else but their eye.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: O ye that know how to weigh your words! study well your audience and suit your speech to it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: 'O ye that have the gift of eloquence ! ascertain the mood of your audience first and then speak after careful deliberation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that take upon themselves to address an assembly without studying its nature: they know not the art of speaking nor are they good for anything else.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Discuss wisdom in the congregation of the wise : but answer fools according to the measure of their folly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the self-control that denieth itself the lead in an assembly of ancients: it is a virtue that outshineth even other virtues.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A failure before men of understanding is like falling off from the way of righteousness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The learning of the scholar shineth forth in all its brilliance only in an assembly of accomplished critics.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Delivering an address of good counsel to men of understanding is like watering the roots of living plants.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: O ye that desire to delight the wise by your discourses ! beware of address-ing even by mistake an audience of fools.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A discourse spoken before the unworthy is like unto ambrosia spilled on filthy ground.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that know how to weigh their words: they will also know how to order their discourse and will not fail before a wise audience.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who can sustain his conclusions in the congregation of the learned: he will be called a scholar among scholars.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They are common, those that can brave death on the battle-field : but they are rare who can face an audience without trembling.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Place before the learned that which thou hast mastered : and that which thou knowest not, learn from them that excel therein.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Master thou the science of reasoning that thou mayest speak without fear in any assembly.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What have they to do with swords, those who have no mettle in them? and what have they to do with books, those who are afraid to face the assembly of the wise?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as the sword in the hand of the eunuch on the battle-field is the learning of him who is afraid to face an audience.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who cannot drive home their point before a learned assembly : even if they possess varied learning they are good for nothing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that possess learning but fear to face an assembly of learned men : they will be esteemed lower than even the ignorant.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that are afraid before an assembly and are unable to expound what they have learned : though they breathe, they are no better than dead men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the great country which never faileth in its yield of harvests, and which is the abode of sages and of rich men that are worthy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the great country which attracteth men to itself by the greatness of its wealth and which yieldeth abundantly for that it is free from pests.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the great nation: even if burdens upon burdens press down upon it, it will support them bravely and pay its taxes in full withal.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the great country which is free from famines and plagues, and which is safe from the invasions of enemies.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the great nation which is not divided into warring sects, which is free from murderous anarchists, and which hath no traitors within its bosom to ruin it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the land that hath known no devastation by its foes, and which, even should it suffer any, would not bate one whit in its yield: it will be called a jewel among the countries of the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The waters of the surface, the waters that flow underground, rain-water, well-situated mountains, and strong fortifications, these are indispensable to every country.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Wealth, richness of yield, happiness, immunity from diseases, and safety from invasions, these five are the ornaments of a kingdom.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That alone deserveth to be called country which produceth abundantly without the labour of the people: that which yieldeth only unto labour deserveth not that name.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if a country hath all these blessings it is worth nothing if it is not blessed in its ruler.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Fortresses are helpful to the weak who are thinking only of their defence : ‘but they are also no less helpful to the strong and powerful.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Water-courses, deserts, mountains, and thick jungles, all these constitute various kinds of defensive barriers.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Height, thickness, strength, and impregnability, these are the four requisites that Science demandeth of fortresses.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the best fortress which is vulnerable in very few places but at the same time is spacious, and which is capable of breaking the assaults of those that attempt to take it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Impregnability, facility of defence for the garrison, and abundance of provisions inside, these are the essential requisites of the fortress.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the real fortress which is filled with stores of every kind and which is garrisoned by men that will make a brave defence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the veritable fortress which cannot be reduced whether by a regular siege or by storm or even by mining.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the veritable fortress which enableth the garrison to defeat the besiegers even when they exert their utmost against it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the veritable fortress which hath been rendered impregnable by works of various kinds, and which enableth the defenders to fell down their adversaries even at the outermost enceintes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: But however strong a fortress may be, it will avail nothing if the defenders show not vigour in action.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is nothing like wealth to lend sO much consequence to men of no consequence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The indigent are decried by all: but every one exalteth the man of substance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The unflickering light called wealth lighteth up all dark places unto him that possesseth it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the substance that is acquired by means that are not evil: righteousness floweth therefrom and happiness also.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Affect not the substance that is divorced from mercy and kindliness, and touch it not with thy hands.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Escheats and derelicts, customs.. duties, and prize acquired in war, all these contribute to build up the wealth of the prince.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Compassion which is the child of Love requireth for tending it the kindly nurse called Wealth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the wealthy man who taketh an enterprise on hand: he is like one-who watcheth an elephant-fight from the top of a hill.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Amass wealth: for there is no sharper steel to cleave thy foeman’s pride.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that hath laid up for himself wealth in great profusion : both the other objects of life are within his reach.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: A well-organised and puissant army that feareth not danger is the first among the possessions of the prince.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is only veterans that can hold out in desperate situations with grim determination, regardless of decimating attacks.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What though they roar even like the ocean ? an army of rats will be annihilated at a single whiff of the cobra’s breath.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That alone deserveth the name of army which knoweth no defeat, which is incapable of being corrupted, and which hath a long tradition of valour behind it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That alone deserveth the name of army which can face valiantly even the God of Death if he should advance against it in all his fury.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Valour, honour, a clear head, and a thorough acquaintance with the history of the great wars of the past, these four are the armours of protection for an army.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That which deserveth the name of army always goeth for the enemy: for it is confident of overcoming him when he offereth battle.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Superiority of armament is a compensation when the army is lacking in dash or steadiness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The army will always win provided that it is not inferior in numbers, hath no implacable jealousies, and is not left to starve without pay.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if there is no lack of troops of the line, there is no army when there are no chiefs to lead.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Face not my master in battle, O ye foes! for many are the men that chal- lenged him and are now lying in stone-marked graves.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The javelin that is aimed at a tusker but misseth bringeth more glory than the arrow that is aimed at a hare and' even hitteth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The furious courage that striketh hard, that is what they call valour: but it is chivalrous generosity to the fallen that giveth it its edge.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The warrior hurled his spear at the elephant and was hurrying back to look for another: but he noticed the spear buried in his own body and smiled with joy as he plucked it out.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is it not a shame to the hero if his eye doth so much as wink when the lance is hurled at him ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The hero counteth those days as wasted on which he receiveth not deep gashes on his body.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that care not for their lives but yearn for the fame that encompasseth the earth about: the anklet that they wear round their foot is a very feast to the eye.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men of valour that fear not for their lives on the battle-field: they forget not their discipline even when their chief is severe upon them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Who hath the right to blame the men who lose their lives in the attempt to accomplish that which they have undertaken ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If one can die so as to draw tears from the eyes of one’s chief, one may even go a-begging in order to obtain for oneself such a death.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is there in the world that is so difficult to acquire as friendship ? and what other armour equalleth it as a defence against the machinations of foes ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Like unto the waxing of the moon is the friendship of the worthy : but the alliance of fools is like the waning thereof.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The friendship of the worthy is like the studying of great books: the more thou approachest them, the more charms thou wilt discover in them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The object of friendship is not merrymaking : but the restraining and reproving of oneself when one goeth astray.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Constant meeting and companionship are superfluous : it is the union of hearts that maketh strong the bond of friendship.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Friendship is not the comradeship that smileth to the face: it is rather the love that delighteth the heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That man alone is thy friend who turneth thee aside from wrong, directeth thee toward the right, and beareth thee company in misfortune.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the hand of the man whose garment hath been blown aside, how it hurrieth to re-cover his limbs: that is the symbol of the true friend that hasteneth to succour a man in his misfortune.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where doth friendship hold its court ? It is where two hearts beat in perfect unison and combine to lift each other up in every possible way.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is beggary in the friendship that can be reckoned, though it boasteth saying, Thus much do I love him and thus much he loveth me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is no greater ill than making a friend without first testing him: for, once a friendship is formed, there is no giving it up for the man of heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that maketh men his friends without previously testing them: he courteth disasters which will only end in his death.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Take into thy consideration the family of the man whom thou desirest to make thy friend, his virtues and his vices, and the whole range of his associates and connexions: and then befriend him if he is worthy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who is born of a good family and who dreadeth disgrace: one ought to acquire his friendship even by paying a price for it if necessary.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Look for the men who know the way of the wise and can reprove and chastise thee whenever thou go astray : and make them thy friends.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a virtue even in misfortune : for it is the rod wherewith to measure thy friends.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To discard the friendship of fools, that is veritable profit for a man.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Think not the thoughts that depress the heart: nor make the friendship of men who will abandon thee the moment thou art down.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The friendship of men that betray in the day of disaster would burn the heart that thinketh on it even at the moment of death.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar
