text: Cultivate with ardour the friendship of the pure: as to men that are unworthy of thee, discard thou their association even if it be by giving them a present.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That friendship is called intimacy which submitteth without resenting to all the freedoms taken by the beloved one.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To be free and easy with each other, that is the heart of true friendship : and it is the part of worthy men never to resent such familiarities.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail is friendship that is longstanding if it acquiesceth not in the liberties taken in its name?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When friends rely on their intimacy and do a thing without leave, the warm-hearted will think of their love and will take it in good part.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When friends do a thing that paineth thee, account thou it as much to their feeling of perfect oneness with thee as to their ignorance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The perfect friend giveth not up the friend of his heart even though he hath been the cause of his ruin.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath loved dearly and long: he bateth not in his affection for his friend even though he cause him damage frequently.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who refuse to listen to any imputations against the friend of their bosom: the day that he doth them an injury is a feast-day unto them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who loveth another with a deathless affection: the whole world will hold him dear.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that alter not in their affection for their old friends : even enemies will look upon them with tenderness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who look as if they would eat thee up for very love, but who love thee not in their hearts: their friendship is sweeter in the waning than in the waxing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the unworthy wretches who would fawn on thee when it is to their profit and forsake thee when thou canst serve them no more: what mattereth it whether thou gain their friendship or lose it ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that calculate how much they can gain by a friend: they are of the same class with harlots and thieves.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There are men who are like the unbroken horse which throweth down its rider on the battle-field and gallopeth away : it is far better to be lonely than to have such men for friends.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the vile men that forsake a trusting friend at the time of his need : it is better not to possess their friendship than to possess it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The enmity of the wise is ten million-times better than the intimacy of fools.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The hate of enemies is a hundred million times more valuable than the friendship of boon companions and flatterers.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that will place obstructions on thy path while thou art at thy work : tell them not a word, but drop their friendship little by little.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose acts belie their spoken words : it is bitter to recall their fellowship even in dreams.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that speak sweet in the closet but disparage in the assembly : do not approach them in any degree.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The friendship that an enemy pretendeth is only an anvil whereon to hammer thee when he seeth his opportunity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who look like friends but are enemies at heart : their friendship will alter even as the heart of a woman.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if his studies are great and godly, it is impossible for an enemy to cast off the hate in his heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Fear thou the hypocritical ruffians that smile to the face but nurse their spite within their bosom.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose hearts are not with thee: though their words tempt thee, place not the slightest faith in them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: An enemy will be revealed in a moment though he speak the tender language of friendship.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Trust not an enemy though he bendeth low in his speech: for the bending of the bow forebodeth nothing but harm.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even in his joined hands thy enemy will have a weapon concealed : nor put thou more faith in his tears.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that make much of thee in public but laugh thee to scorn in secret : humour thou them openly but crush them even in the embrace of friendship.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When thou canst not yet break openly with thy foe, feign friendship to his face but keep him off from thy heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Dost thou want to know what folly is? It is the throwing away of that which is profitable and the holding fast to that which is hurtful.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The chiefest among all kinds of folly is the folly of inclining the heart towards conduct that is unbecoming to oneself.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fool is neglectful of duties and rude of speech, and callous to all sense of shame: and he will cherish nothing that is good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a man that is learned and subtle and a teacher of others, and yet continueth to be the slave of his passions himself : there is no greater fool than he.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fool hath the gift of sowing in one birth the seeds of misery for all his future incarnations.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the fool that taketh in his hand an enterprise of moment: he will not merely spoil it, he will qualify also for fetters.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the fool should come by a great fortune it is strangers that will feast and his kindred will only starve.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the fool obtaineth anything of value he will behave like a madman who is also grown tipsy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Greatly delectable is the friendship of fools : one feeleth no pangs when one parteth from them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as is the placing of an unwashed foot on the couch, even so is the entrance of the fool in an assembly of men of worth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The veritable poverty is the poverty of sense: the world regardeth not other poverty as poverty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When a fool bestoweth a gift of his own free will, it is simply the good fortune of the receiver and nothing else.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The troubles that a fool bringeth down on his head, it is hard even for his enemies to cause him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Dost thou want to know what is shallowness of wit? It is the conceit that sayeth to itself, I am wise.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the fool that pretendeth unto knowledge that he possesseth not : he raiseth doubts even as to those things that he really knoweth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where is the good of the fool covering his nakedness, if the deformities of his mind are still left uncovered ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the shallow man that cannot keep a secret to himself: he will bring down great calamities on his own head.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who neither listeneth to advice nor knoweth for himself what is right : all the days of his life he is a plague to his fellows.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He that trieth to open the eyes of a fool is a fool himself : for the fool seeth but one way and that way is never wrong in his eyes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who denieth what all the world doth assert: he will be looked upon as a devil in human shape.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The spirit of defiance is the peccant humour which developpeth in all men the distemper called hate.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even when thy neighbour injureth thee with the deliberate purpose of picking a quarrel, even then it is best not to harbour vengeance or return the injury.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The habit of defying others is verily a grievous malady: if a man freeth himself from it, he will acquire everlasting fame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The highest joys will be within thy reach if thou reject from thy heart that greatest of evils, the defiant spirit.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Who can desire the overthrow of the man who hath the talent to avoid hostilities ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who taketh delight in breathing defiance against his neighbours: it will not be long before he doth stumble and fall.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince of spiteful nature who is ever addicted to strife: he will be blind to the policy that advanceth nations.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The avoiding of strife leadeth unto prosperity : but if thou allow it to grow apace, ruin will not lag far behind.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When fortune is about to smile on a man he will ignore all provocation: but when Destiny hath decreed him ruin, he will set no bounds to his defiance of his neighbours.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: From defiance springeth all that is bitter: but good-will yieldeth the glorious fruit of peace and harmony.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Strive not with the powerful : but against those that are weaker than thyself carry on wars without relaxing even for one moment.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who is cruel, and who hath neither allies nor the strength to stand alone : how is he going to withstand his enemy’s forces ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a prince that hath neither courage nor understanding nor liberality, and yet will not live in peace with his neighbours: he is an easy prey to his foes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who is always ill-tempered and who controlleth not his tongue : he will be an easy prey to everybody at all times and at all places.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a prince who is tactless, who careth not for honour, and who neglecteth the science of politics and the works that it enjoineth: verily he is a joy unto his enemies.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who is a slave to his lust and who loseth his reason in the blindness of rage: his enmity will be welcomed by his foes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who undertaketh an enterprise but doth things that accord not with its success: verily one should seek his enmity even by paying a price for it if necessary.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a prince hath no virtues and many vices he will have no allies and his enemies will rejoice.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Enemies rejoice exceedingly when they get a fool and a coward to contend against.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince who careth not even to fight his foolish neighbour and obtain an easy victory : glory will reject him for evermore.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The accursed thing called enmity should never be courted willingly even though it be only in jest.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if thou challenge the men whose weapon is the bow, provoke not the men whose weapon is their tongue.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince that hath no allies but challengeth to war a multitude of foes: he is more insane than even a madman.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the prince that hath the tact to convert enemies into allies: his power will last without end.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou hast to contend alone and without allies against two enemies, try to gain over one of them to thy side.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whether thou hast decided to make a neighbour thy friend or thine enemy, do not make him either when thou art embarrassed, but leave him alone.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Reveal not thy troubles to men who know it not ; neither expose thy weak-nesses to thine enemies.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Form a wise plan, consolidate thy resources, and provide for thy defences : if thou do this, it will not be long before the pride of thy enemies is humbled to the dust.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Fell down thorn-trees while yet they are young: for when they are overgrown they will themselves cut the hand that attempteth to fell them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily thy shall not last long, those who humble not the pride of men who defy them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even groves and fountains give no joy if they breed disease : even so kinsmen too are an abomination when they seek one’s ruin.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Fear not the foe that is like the naked sword: but beware of the enemy that cometh as a friend.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Guard thyself against the secret enemy: for in the moment of embarrassment he will cut thee clean like the potter’s steel.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou have an enemy that masque-radeth about as thy friend, he will soon corrupt thy kindred and bring down a multitude of evils on thy head.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When a kinsman turneth traitor against thee, he will bring on thee a multitude of evils and jeopardise thy very life.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When treachery invadeth the entourage of the prince, it is impossible that he falleth not a prey to it one day or other.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The house that is divided against itself is like a vessel that is fitted with a lid: though it appeareth to be a single unit, it will never make a united whole.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the house that is divided against itself: it will crumble to dust even like a piece of iron that is filed with a file.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though the split be small even like a slit in a sesamum seed, ruin hangeth over the house that is divided against itself.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who mixeth on intimate terms with one who hateth him in his heart : he is like one dwelling in a hut with a cobra for his companion.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The greatest care of a man that looketh to his safety should be to guard himself carefully from offending the Great Ones.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man slighteth the Great Ones, their power will bring down on him miseries without end.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Dost thou seek thy annihilation? then close thy ears to good counsel and offer provocation to men who have the power to destroy thee when they please.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the weak man slighting men of might and power: it is as if he beckoneth to the God of Death to come to him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who provoke the wrath of princes of the mighty arm: wheresoever they go they will not thrive.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even men who are caught in a conflagration may escape alive: but there is no safety for men who wrong the mighty ones.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where will be thy life with its varied glories and thy wealth with all its splendour, if sages, strong in the strength of the spirit, are incensed against thee ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the princes who look as if they are established on an everlasting foundation : even they will perish with all their kin if men who are mighty as the mountain but will their doom.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even the king of the Gods will fall from his place and lose his sovereignty if men of holy vows look on him in anger.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even men who rest upon the most solid of supports will not be saved if men of great spiritual power frown on them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that dote upon their wives will not attain to greatness: those that have the ambition to do great things turn away from such seduction.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath an abject infatuation for his wife: in the very midst of his prosperity he will be a by-word among men, and he will have to hide his face in shame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The weakling who humbleth himself before his wife will always be ashamed to show his face before the worthy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the salvation-less wretch that trembleth before his wife: his talents will never be held in any esteem.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man who feareth his wife will never have the courage to do a service even to the worthy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who stand in awe of the tender arms of their wives: though they live like Gods no man will respect them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that submitteth to petticoat government: a bashful maid hath more dignity in her than he.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that allow themselves to be governed by their wives ; they will not satisfy the wants of their friends, neither will they do anything that is good.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that submit to petticoat government : neither righteousness nor wealth nor even the joy of love will be found with them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose thoughts are set on great affairs and who are the favourites of fortune : they yield not to the folly of doting on their wives.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the women that desire a man for the sake of his gold and not for the sake of love: their cajoleries will lead only to misery.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the women who speak honeyed words, but whose thoughts are ever fixed on their own profit : consider their ways and keep them at a distance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The prostitute pretendeth love when she embraceth her lover: but in her heart she feeleth even as one who hath touched a stranger dead body in a dark room.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose hearts are inclined to deeds of purity: they defile themselves not with the touch of harlots.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who add deep study toa clear understanding: they defile themselves not with the touch of women whose charms are free to all.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that have a regard for their own good: they touch not the hand of wantons who put up their lewd charms for sale.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who are _light-minded: they will seek the women who embrace with the body while their heart is somewhere else.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who have not a discriminating understanding : the embraces of wily women are to them even as the fascination of the siren of the solitudes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The soft arms of the well-decked harlot are the filthy ditch wherein contemptible fools drown themselves.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Women of two hearts, drink, and the dice-table, these are the delights of men when fortune forsaketh them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who are addicted to drink: they will never be feared by their enemies, and even the glory they have acquired they will lose.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let none drink: but if they desire, let those men drink who care not for the esteem of worthy men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The sight of the man who is intoxicated is an abomination even unto his own mother: what must it be then to the worthy ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who is addicted to the low vice of drunkenness: the fair one called Shame turneth her back upon him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is the veriest idiocy to spend one’s substance and obtain in return only insensibility.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who drink the poison ‘called toddy day after day: they are as men that are asleep, neither do they differ from dead men.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who drink in secret and pass their days in torpid insensibility: their neighbours will soon find them out, and hold them in utter contempt.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let not the drunkard pretend, saying. I know not even what it is to be drunk : for thereby he would merely add falsehood to his other vice.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who reproveth one who is intoxicated: he is like a man who searcheth torch in hand one who is immersed under water.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man who seeth while he is sober the drunken state of another man, cannot he picture to himself his own state when he is drunk?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Take not to gambling even if thou win : for thy wins are even as the baited hook that the fish swalloweth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the gamblers who lose a hundred where they gain but one: is there forsooth a way even for them to thrive in the world ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man bet constantly over dice, his substance will only go into stranger hands.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Nothing bringeth on wretchedness so surely as gambling : for it killeth a man’s good name and driveth his heart to every ignoble deed.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Many there have been who were proud of their skill in the throwing of dice and were mad after the gambling-house: but there hath not been a single man of them that did not come to grief.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that are blinded by the Genius of Wretchedness who cometh in the form of a passion for gambling: they will starve and suffer every misery.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou throw away thy time at the gambling-house, thy inheritance will be consumed and thy fair name will be wiped out.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Gambling will consume thy substance and corrupt thy honesty: it will harden thy heart and bring on thee misery.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Glory, learning, wealth, and even food and clothing will depart from the man who betaketh himself to gambling.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The passion for gambling increaseth with the losses incurred in the bettings: even so doth the craving of the soul for life grow with the griefs that it suffereth therein.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Every one of the three humours described by sages, beginning with the windy one, would cause disease whenever they go to either extreme.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The body requireth no medicine if new food is eaten only after the old food is fully digested.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Eat with moderation and after the food that thou hast taken is digested : that is the way to prolong thy days.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Wait till thy food is digested and thy appetite is keen: then eat moderately the food that agreeth with thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou eat abstemiously the food that doth not disagree with thee thou wilt have no troubles in the body.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as Health seeketh the man who eateth only when his stomach is empty, even so doth Disease seek the man who eateth to excess.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who glutteth himself foolishly beyond the measure of his internal heat : his diseases will exceed all measure.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Consider the disease and its origin and the means of curing it: and then set about the cure with every precaution.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let the physician take the measure of the patient and the disease and the season that is: and then let him undertake the cure.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The patient, the physician, the medicine, and the apothecary, on these four doth all cure depend: and four again are the attributes of each of them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Rectitude and a sense of shame come by nature only to men who are born of a good family.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Men of family fall not from three things, namely, correct conduct, truth, and a sense of shame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Four are the attributes of the true gentleman: a smiling face, a liberal hand, sweetness of speech, and condescension.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Men of family would not tarnish their name even for the sake of tens of millions.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men of ancient family : they give not up their liberality even when their means of munificence are diminished.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who are anxious to keep pure the honourable traditions of their family: they will never take to deceit nor descend to ignoble deeds.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fault of a man of noble family will show conspicuously even as the spot in the body of the moon.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If rudeness of speech showeth itself in a man coming of a good family, people would even suspect the legitimacy of his descent.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The nature of a soil is known by the seedling that groweth therein: even so is the family of a man known by the words that come out of his mouth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou desire virtue, thou must cultivate the sense of shame: and if thou want to honour thy family, thou must be respectful unto all.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Forbear from those things that would lower thee, even though they should be indispensable for the very preservation of thy life.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that desire to leave an honoured name behind them: they will not do that which is not right even for the sake of glory.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Cultivate modesty in the day of prosperity : but in the day of thy decline hold fast to thy dignity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that have soiled a name that was honourable: they are even as the locks of hair that have been shaven off the head and thrown away.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even men who are grand as a mountain will look small if they do an ignoble thing, though it should be only of the measure of a kunri seed.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It bringeth not glory, neither doth it open the way unto heaven: why then doth a man try to live by fawning on men that despise him ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is better for a man to meet his doom at once without any ado than to maintain himself by hanging on to those that scorn him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is the skin immortal, that men desire: to save it even at the cost of honour ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The kavarima giveth up its life when it loseth its wool: there are men who are as sensitive and they put an end to their lives when they cannot save their honour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men of honour who refuse to outlive their good name: the world will join its hands and worship at the altar of their glory.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: An aspiration for noble achievement, that is what is called greatness: and littleness is the thought that sayeth, I shall live without it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The manner of birth is the same for all men: but their reputations vary because they differ in the lives that they lead.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if they are noble, those that are not noble are not noble; and even if they are low-born, those that are not low are not low.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as chastity in a woman, greatness can be maintained only by being true to one’s own self.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Those that are great have the puissance to employ adequate means and achieve things that are impossible for others.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is not in the grain of small men to revere the great and earn their good will and favour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If fortune falleth to the lot of the little-minded their insolence will know no bounds.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Greatness is ever unpretending and modest: but littleness vaunteth its merits before all the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Greatness showeth condescension unto all: but littleness is the very acme of insolence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Greatness is always for screening the infirmities of others: but littleness will: talk nothing but scandal.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that know their duties and want to cultivate worth in themselves: everything that is good will be a duty in their eyes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The comeliness of the worthy is the comeliness of their character: the comeliness of the body addeth nothing to their comeliness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Love to all, sensibility to shame, complaisance, indulgence to the faults of others, and truthfulness, these five are the pillars that support the edifice of a noble character.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The virtue of the saint is non-killing : and the virtue of the worthy man is the abstaining from scandalous speech.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is humility that is the strength of the strong: and that is also the armour of the man of worth against his foes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is the touchstone of worth ? It is the acknowledgement of superiority when it is found even in men who are otherwise one’s inferiors.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where is the superiority of the worthy man if he doth not do good even unto those that work him injury ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Poverty is no disgrace to a man if he possesseth the wealth that is called character.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that would not swerve from the path of rectitude even if all else should change in a general convulsion: they will be called the very palladium of worth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily even the earth itself will not be able to support the burden of human life if the worthy were to fall from their worth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Courteousness, they say, cometh easily to those who receive all men with open arms.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Courteousness cometh of the combination of the two virtues of kindness and good-breeding.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Men are likened to each other not by the cut of their personal appearance, but by the similarity of their manners.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who love justice and righteousness, and who are of a helpful disposition: the world setteth a high value on their manners.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Disparaging words pain a man even when uttered only in jest: the well-bred therefore are never discourteous even to their foes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The world goeth on smoothly because of the men of good-breeding : verily, but for them all this harmony would be dead and buried in the dust.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though they are sharp as files, the men that are lacking in good manners are no better than mere wooden stocks.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Discourtesy is unbecoming in a man, even were it only against men who are unfriendly and unjust.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men who cannot smile: in all the wide, wide world they will see nothing but darkness even during the day.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the wealth in the hands of the churlish man : it is even as the milk that is spoiled for being kept in an unclean vessel.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who hath laid by in his home treasures in abundance but enjoyeth them not: he is as good as dead, for he maketh no use of them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the miser that thinketh that wealth is all in all and hoardeth it without giving to any : he will be a demon in his next birth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that are always after hoarding but care not for fame: their existence is a burden unto the earth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man who careth not to earn the attachment of his neighbours, what doth he hope to leave behind him when he is dead ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that neither give unto others nor enjoy their wealth themselves: even if they possess tens of millions they really possess nothing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a man that enjoyeth not his wealth nor giveth freely to men of worth: he is a disease unto a great fortune.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that giveth not anything to the needy: the wealth in his hands is like a fair damsel that wasteth away her youth in loneliness.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fortune of the man that is not loved of men is like the fruiting of the poison tree in the midst of the village.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The wealth that is made without any regard to love or righteousness, and by starving oneself, is hoarded only for the behoof of strangers.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The distress of the man of wealth who hath emptied his resources by bene-factions is only like the exhaustion of the rain-cloud ; it will not continue for long.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The blush of the worthy is for action that become them not: it is therefore quite different to the blush of the fair.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Food, clothing, and progeny are common unto all men : it is in the sensibility to shame that they differ from one another.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The body is the seat of all life: but a virtuous blush is the dwelling place of worth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is not the jewel of the worthy their sense of shame ? And when a man hath it not, is not his swagger an affliction unto the eye to behold ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that blush as much for others’ disgrace as for their own: they will be called the very dwelling place of delicacy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The worthy refuse to acquire even kingdoms save by means for which they shall not have to blush.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that have a delicate sense of shame: they will renounce their lives to save themselves from a disgrace, but will not swallow their shame even in order to save their lives.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If a man blush not for those things that call forth a blush in others, Righteousness will have cause to blush for him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: By neglecting ceremonial observances a man loseth only his family : but every good is lost when he is lost to shame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The men that are dead to shame live not: they merely feign life even as wooden marionettes that are moved by strings.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Nothing advanceth a man’s family so much as his determination never to weary in labouring with his hands.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Manly exertion and a sound understanding: it is the fulness of these two that exalteth the family.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When a man setteth out saying, I shall advance my house, the very Gods gird up their loins and march before him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that remit not in their exertions to raise high their family: the work of their hands will prosper of itself even if they make no elaborate plans therefor.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man that setteth his family on high without doing iniquity : the whole world will be asa kindred unto him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: That is the supreme manhood which bringeth to a high estate the family wherein one is born.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as the brunt of an action falleth on the courageous on the battle-field, even so the burden of keeping up the family lieth only on the shoulders of those that can bear the burden.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is no season for them that desire the advancement of their family : if they take things easy or stand upon their dignity, their house will be brought low.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily, is the body of the man that would protect his family against every ill a receptacle for toils and hardships alone ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the family that hath no goodman to prop it up: calamities will gnaw into its roots and it will fall to the ground.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Roam where they will, men must at last stand behind the plough for their food : in spite of every hardship, therefore, husbandry is the chiefest industry.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Husbandmen are the linch-pin of society : for they support all those that take to other work, not having the strength to plough.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They alone live who live by tilling the ground: all others eat only the bread of dependence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men whose fields sleep under the shadow of the rich ears of their harvests: they will see the umbrellas of other princes bow down before the umbrella of their own sovereign.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that eat the bread of husbandry: they will not only not beg themselves, but they will also give alms to those that beg, without ever Saying nay.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even they who have renounced all desire will have to suffer if the husbandman sitteth still with folded arms.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou dry the soil of thy field till an ounce of mould is reduced to a quarter-ounce of dust, then not even a handful of manure will be needed, and the yield would be abundant.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Manuring profiteth more than the ploughing: and when the land is weeded, guarding it profiteth more than irrigation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the goodman visiteth not his land but sitteth at home, the land will take huff even as the goodwife.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The fair one called Earth laugheth to herself when she seeth the sluggard cry, saying, Alas, I have nothing to eat.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Wantest thou to know what is more galling than indigence ? then know that indigence alone is more galling than indigence.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Caitiff Indigence is an enemy to the joys of this life as well as of the next.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The itching that goeth by the name of Indigence killeth dignity of demeanour and refinement of speech, even though they run in the very blood.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Want will drive even men of high family to forget their dignity and to speak the language of abject servility.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There are a thousand mortifications concealed underneath this one curse called poverty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The words of the indigent will carry no weight even when they expound grand truths with masterly skill and knowledge.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The poverty that is divorced from virtue will estrange even the mother that bore him from the side of the miserable wretch.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is Indigence to bear me company even to-day ? It tormented me but only yesterday even unto death.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is possible to go to sleep even in the midst of flames : but it is impossible to get even a wink of sleep in the midst of poverty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The one way open to the indigent is to renounce utterly, their lives: their not doing so is but death to salt and rice- water.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou mayest beg if thou seest men that can afford to do charity: if they feign inability, it is their fault, not thine.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even begging will be a pleasure if thou canst obtain what thou beggest without suffering any humiliation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a charm even in begging; at the hands of those who understand their duty and do not falsely pretend inability to help.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the man who sayeth not nay to a request even in a dream: begging at the hands of such a man is as honourable as bestowing itself.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If men take freely to begging asa means of livelihood, it is because there are men in the world that refuse not alms.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that have not the churlishness to deny charity : the pangs of poverty would cease at the very sight of them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the men that give without snubbing or huffing the beggar: the heart of the beggar rejoiceth when he meeteth them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If there were none to beg for alms, the whole world would have no more interest than a dance of marionettes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where would be the glory of men Of a liberal hand if there were none in the world to beg of them ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let not the beggar scowl when a man pleadeth inability to give: for his own need should be enough to show him that another may be in like condition.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The man that beggeth not is ten million times worthier than he that beggeth, even though it be only at the hands of men that give lovingly and with all their heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If He that made the earth intended that man should live even by begging, may He wander about the world and perish.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Nothing is hardier than the hardihood that sayeth to itself, I shall put an end to my indigence by begging.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the dignity that consenteth not to beg even when reduced to utter destitution: even the whole universe is too small to hold it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though it is only gruel thin as water, nothing is more savoury than the food that is earned by the labour of one’s hands.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if what thou beggest is only water for the cow, nothing is so humiliating to the tongue to utter as a begging prayer.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of all that beg I shall beg but this one thing: If ye needs must beg, beg not of those that shirk.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The hapless ship called begging will split the moment that it striketh the rock of dodging.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The heart melteth even when it contemplateth the lot of the beggar: but when it thinketh on the rebuffs that He receiveth, it simply dieth away.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Where doth the life of the dodger hide itself when he sayeth nay? At the mere sound of his rebuff the life of the beggar ebbeth away !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How they take after men, these degraded ones ! We have never seen likeness so exact!
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Happier than men of conscience are these despicable ones! For they never have any pangs of the mind to feel.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Like unto very Gods are the base ones on earth ! For they too are a law unto themselves.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When the degenerate meeteth a reprobate, he would outbeat him in his vices and pride himself on the achievement.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Fear is the only motive force of degenerates: if there is any other at all, it is appetite, and it availeth just a little.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Like unto a tomtom are the base ones: for they cannot rest without giving out to others the secrets that are entrusted to them.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The degenerate would grudge even to jerk his hands moistened with food, save to those that can break his jaw with clenched fists.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The worthy can be commanded by a simple word: but, like the sugar-cane, the low can be made to give only by a sound thrashing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is enough if he seeth a neighbour clothed and fed: the vile man can always discover vices in his character.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is the resource of the degene-. rate when misfortune befalleth him ? He hath but one, and that is to sell himself as quickly as possible.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The jewelled form that appeareth yonder, is it a Goddess? or a peacock chosen from among its kind? or is it simply a lovely maid? Verily I am too dazed to tell.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How would it fare with men if the fascinating siren of the solitudes assail them with a whole host behind her? So fareth it with me when the lovely one returneth my look.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I never knew Death before: I know it now : it weareth the form of a woman and hath large and battling eyes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: She is simple and gracious, but yet her eyes are versed in the ways of waging war: for they drink the lives of those that look on her.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is it Death that I behold or simply eyes ? or is it the look of the gazelle ? for all three are to be found in the glance of this artless one.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is only when her eyebrows will cease to bend and will veil her looks that her eyes will cease to cause me the pangs that make me tremble.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The vestment that covereth the beauteous breasts of this fair one are even as the eye-cover on the eyes of the infuriate elephant.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is it by her fair forehead that my manhood is overcome, the manhood that causeth to tremble even those that have not faced me on the battle-field ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To what end are these trinkets that merely mar her beauty, when she hath the guileless look of the fawn and modesty as her especial ornaments ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Wine giveth joy, but only to him that tasteth it : it can never delight at the mere seeing as doth love.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Two are the looks of her eye: one of them tortureth the heart, but the other is the balm that healeth it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The furtive lightning glance that is turned on the lover the moment that his eyes are turned aside, is not merely the half of love: it is more than a moiety.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: She looked, and then she bowed: that was the watering of the young plant of love that was springing between us.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When I look at her, she looketh at the ground: but when I look away, she looketh on me and softly smileth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: She doth not seem to see me, it is true: but she smileth to me the while she affecteth but to wink an eye.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though they feign to speak as strangers, the words of the loving will be seen through in an instant.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The half-hearted reproach and the offended look are the marks of those who pretend to spurn but who really love us in their hearts.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The slender-shaped maid melteth to see my imploring look and_ softly smileth: and the gentle smile giveth her an added grace.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is only in lovers’ eyes that one can see the look of absolute unconcern, as if they were perfect strangers.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When eyes speak their consent to eyes, the words of the mouth are quite superfluous.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: All the delights of sight and sound and smell and taste and touch are to be found in their entirety only in this damsel of the shining bangles.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The cure of all disease lieth in some other thing than that which causeth it: but the pang that this damsel causeth, she alone can heal.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is the world of the lotus-eyed God sweeter than the tender arms of her that one loveth ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When she is ata distance she burneth, but when she is near she is refreshingly cool: ah! whence did she obtain this strange fire ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Behold the witchery of my love whose tresses are adorned with flowers ! whatever thing my heart desireth, that very thing her form seemeth to me to be !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of ambrosia are the arms of my artless damsel formed: for their every touch reviveth my dying limbs.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The embrace of this lovely fair is supremely joyous, even as the family life of the householder who eateth his portion only after distributing charity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Joyous to the loving pair is the embrace that alloweth not even the air to come between.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The pettish frown, the softening of the heart, and the new embrace, these are the sweets that lovers enjoy.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as a man feeleth his ignorance the more keenly the more wise he groweth, even so do I love her the more ardently, the more I enjoy her company.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Soft art thou, O blest anitcha flower ! but tenderer than thyself is she on whom my heart is set.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou becomest distracted whenever thou seest a flower, O my Heart! Thou thinkest that the flowers that look on all men can resemble her eye !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Her arm is as the bamboo; her body is as the tender leaf; her smile is a very pearl; the sweetest of odours is in her breath ; and her eye is piercing as the lance.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The sky-blue flower despaireth of ever equalling her eye in beauty, and droopeth down its head whenever it looketh on her.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: She hath adorned herself with anitcha flowers but hath not removed the stems from among them: alack! her waist will be crushed beneath the weight and will presently break !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The stars of the heavens wander from their spheres for that they cannot tell which is the moon and which her face.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: But is there a spot in the face of this fair one even as in the moon which hath rounded up only to-day its deformities of yesterday ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bless thee, O Moon! If thou canst shine like the face of this lovely one, I shall love thee in very truth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou want, O Moon, to emulate the face of her whose eyes are like flowers, show not thyself unto all but shine alone for me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even the anitcha flower and swan’s down are as nettle to the feet of this fair one.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as honey and milk mingled together is the dew on the lips of this fair one with the subdued speech.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How great is the love between the body and the soul? Even so great is my love for this artless one.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: O thou Image in the pupil of mine eye! Leave and give room to the fair one that I love, for there is no other abode that is worthy of her.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is as life when she is near : but it is as very death when she leaveth my side.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The virtues of this maiden of the fair and battling eyes I certainly can remember, provided first I can forget them: but how to forget them I know not!
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He will not go from my eyes, neither will he be hurt when I wink: so subtle is the form of my beloved.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My beloved dwelleth ever within my eyes; so I do not paint them even lest I lose sight of him even for an instant.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My beloved is ever in my heart: so I eat not hot food lest it burn him there.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I wink not for fear that I should lose sight of him even for that instant : and for this the village folk charge him with cruelty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He dwelleth lovingly within my bosom and is never away from thence: and yet the village folk declare that he hath abandoned me, and call him cruel.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To those who are torn from their loved one and suffer the pangs of their passion there is no other resource left but the riding of the palmyra stalk.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Body and soul cannot support this anguish and have consented to ride the palm: they have trampled down all shame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Firmness and delicacy I had formerly: but now I possess only the stalk of the palmyra that is ridden by the love-lorn lover.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I put my trust on the raft that was built of firmness and delicacy : but the rushing stream of passion hath carried it along in its course.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: This fair one who weareth tiny bracelets and who is tender as a flower, it is she that hath given me the palm-stalk and the anguish of eventide.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My eyes cannot sleep for thinking of that artless one: I shall ride the stalk therefore even in this late hour of the night.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Nothing is grander than the woman who refuseth to ride the palm-stalk even when the passion of her heart is deep as the ocean.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My Passion considereth not the strength of my modesty nor my kindness towards itself, and betrayeth my secret by showing itself abroad.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My passion seeth that none taketh notice of it: and it wandereth about In the streets in great anguish.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Fools laugh at me to my very face: for they have not felt all the pangs that I feel.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: As the outcry riseth in the village my life cometh back to me: it Is my good luck that many do not know this secret.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: These village folk know not the rare virtues of my beloved with the flowerlike eyes: for they have given her cheaply to me by raising this clamour.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is not this gossip of the village a precious thing unto me? for even without obtaining her I feel as if I possess her already.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: This clamour hath increased my passion for her: without it it would have been but a stale affair.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as every cup that is drunk but maketh the drunkard thirst for more, even so doth every discovery of his passion by others but increase its sweetness for the lover.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Our meeting was but for one day: but the outcry that hath arisen over it is as when the serpent hath swallowed the moon !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The public talk is the manure, and the reproach of mother is the water, that unite to feed and prolong this anguish.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To think of extinguishing my passion by raising this clamour Is like wanting to put out a fire by pouring ghee over it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is it forme to blush at this outcry now, when he who said, Fear not, hath abandoned me to the scandal of every by-stander ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: This clamour which I in my heart so much desire, the village rabble hath raised for me: verily my beloved will not refuse it me if I should beg it of him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If there is anything about not parting, speak it tome: but if it is only thy quick return, tell it to those who will survive till then.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: His mere look was once a delight unto me: but now even his embrace saddeneth, for that I fear that he is to part.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is impossible to put trust in any, seeing that the thought of separation lurketh somewhere even in the heart of him who knoweth my heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If he who bade me be of good cheer consenteth to part from me, can I be blamed for having placed my trust in his solemn promise ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou wouldst save my life, O my maid, prevent the master of that life, from going: for if he part from me, I despair of our meeting again.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When he hath the hardness to say to my very face, I shall depart, I give up all hope of his ever coming back to save me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Would not my close-fitting bracelets themselves that have slipped from my wrists raise the bruit of the parting of my lord?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bitter is life in a place where there are no bosom friends: but bitterer far is separation from the beloved one.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Hath fire, which burneth only when it is touched the power, like love, to burn when it is far away?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Many there are, are there not, who live through the pangs of leave-taking and of separation, and survive till the return of the beloved !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I smother my grief within me, but behold! it only welleth up more and more even as the water of the spring to those who are draining it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To conceal my grief is now beyond me: but as to disclosing it, I should feel ita shame to speak of it even to him that caused it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: At the two ends of the pole which is my life, my two loads of passion and delicacy hang heavy; and this suffering body breaketh under their weight.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a very sea before me in my passion for my beloved: but a trusty bark to cross it there is none for me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What will they not do when they are enemies, those who suffer one to pine away when they are friends ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Vast as the sea is the joy that love yieldeth: but when it taketh to burning, the pangs it causeth are deeper far.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I swim in the stormy sea of love, but I spy not any shore thereto: even in the dead of night I am all alone and there is none to console me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Night in her mercy rocketh all life to sleep: and yet she hath none to help her through but me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The Night that passeth too slowly for me to-day is crueller in its cruelty than the cruel one himself.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If my eyes can run, even as my heart runneth, to where he is, they need not now be swimming in a sea of tears.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Why do my Eyes complain to me to-day ? This inconsolable grief hath come even upon me only through their showing to me my beloved.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How is it that the Eyes that looked rashly on the beloved that day grieve to-day, instead of bearing patiently the consequences of their own folly ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They looked on him straightway of their own free will that day, and to-day they weep of themselves: how they make themselves ridiculous!
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: After bequeathing to me the incurable grief that consumeth me, my Eyes have now dried up, having exhausted their store of tears.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My Eyes which have brought on me this anguish vaster than the ocean, now pine away with grief and cannot even lay themselves to sleep.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Oh, it is a sweet revenge to me that the Eyes that caused me this sorrow are victims themselves to the self-same anguish!
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Beshrew the eyes that hung upon his form on that day with a passionate, greedy, all-absorbing love! May they dry up to their very roots with pining and repining !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily there be those who love without being loved! For here are my eyes which know no repose for not seeing him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My Eyes sleep not when he is away, neither sleep they when he is returned: either way it is their lot to suffer unceasing pain.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When people’s eyes themselves are tell-tale drums, even as my own, it Is not hard for strangers to read the secret they seek to conceal.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is I myself that consented to the parting of my beloved: to whom shall I complain now of my pallor?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Pallor is proud of being his child, and creeping all over my frame rideth on me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My comeliness and my modesty he hath taken away, giving in exchange nought but the pangs of the heart and my pallid hue.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: In my heart I think nought but his thoughts, with my tongue I speak nought but his praises: and yet, witchcraft ! this pallor hath overspread my frame.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar
