text: That day too he went but there, and paleness sought me out here!
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as darkness lieth in wait for the light to be put out, even so doth Pallor lie in wait for my separation from my lord.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I lay in his embrace: I then left him for a while, and behold, pallor swallowed me up, as it were !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There are people to reproach me saying, Behold she hath become sallow and pale: but there is none to reproach him for abandoning me !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Acquit him forsooth, my maid, of all harmful intent : the death-like pallor of my body is nothing to thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is good for me even to be twitted with the sallowness of my skin, if only they accuse not my beloved of cruelty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They alone eat the stoneless all-sweet fruit of love who are beloved of those whom they hold dear.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What the rain is to all the world, that is the tenderness of the beloved to her that loveth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They alone can pride themselves on their happiness who are loved in return by those whom they love.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What if they are loved by others? If women receive not the affection of their beloved they know, no happiness on earth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How can I hope for any favour from my beloved if he loveth me not even as I love him ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as the burthen on the carrying pole, love is pleasant only when it is on both sides: but it is a galling load when it is only on one side.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The God of Love assaileth only me: is it because he hath no eyes for my sorrows and sufferings ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: None in the world are so hard-hearted as women who continue to live on even when they receive no kind messages from their beloved.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if the beloved is unkind to us, any message that cometh from him is sweet to the ear.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bless thee, my Heart! Thou wouldst tell thy grief to one who loveth thee not : thou mayest as well try to dry up the sea.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even in the recollection love is sweet with endless delights: love is therefore sweeter than wine.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The moment I recall the image of my loved one to my mind, that very moment all my sorrow is vanquished : ah, love is dear in all its aspects !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I was about to sneeze, but the fit passed away : is it that he was about to think of me but did not ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Have I at all a place in his heart ? As for him, there is never a doubt but he abideth in mine.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He excludeth me jealously from his heart : is he not ashamed then to show himself ceaselessly in mine ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is but the recollection of our union that keepeth me alive yet : what else of life is there in me ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even with my memory full of him,. my heart burneth within me: what then will be my case if I forget him ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How often soever I recall my beloved to my mind he will not be wroth with me: so much is the favour that my beloved bestoweth upon me !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When my heart thinketh on his cruelty who once said, We are not two but only one life and soul, verily my life ebbeth away.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: O Moon! set not in the horizon, I pray thee, till my eyes look again upon him who, abiding still within my heart,. hath yet parted from me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What honours shall I do to the Dream which hath brought me a message from the beloved ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If only I could persuade my eyes to sleep, I would fly to my beloved in my dream, and tell him the story of how I manage yet to hold on to life.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If I am able to support life yet it is only because I see him in dreams who showeth not his face in waking hours.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Dream giveth me all the joys of love: for it bringeth back to me my beloved who refuseth to pity me in my waking state.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The joys of the dream last as long as the beloved appeareth in it: and what more can be said of the waking state?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Oh that there were no waking state ! For then my dream would never be cut short and my beloved would never depart from me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The cruel one who pitieth me not while I am awake, why doth he haunt me in my dreams ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He embraceth me while I am asleep and rusheth into my heart as soon as I open my eyes.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They reproach my beloved for that he doth not meet me to their knowledge: but then they see him not in dreams.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: These village folk say that he hath parted from me: is it that they see him not in dreams?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Evening ! Bless thee, but who calleth thee Evening ? Thou art really the hour that devoureth the lives of the wedded ones !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou lookest melancholy and pale, O Eventide! Pray, tell me, dear, is thy lover also cruel even as mine?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The dewy evening hour that once used to come trembling and sighing before me, now advanceth boldly, bringing nought but grief and despair unto my heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When the beloved is away, evening approacheth even as the executioner advancing to the execution-ground.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What is the kindness that I had done to the morning hour? and how have I injured eventide ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Alack the day! I never knew the sting of the evening so long as my beloved was by my side.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: This sickness buddeth in the morning, goeth on opening its petals the livelong day, and standeth full-blown at eventide.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: They call it the pipe of the shepherd, but verily it is a murderous weapon tome : for it ushereth in the evening that burneth me so.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If evening that hath already driven me mad should advance any further,. the whole town will be shrouded in sorrow before long, for I shall simply die.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The life which is yet clinging on to me will soon depart : for eventide recalleth to me the image of him who, is mad after wealth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My eyes think on him who left me saying that it was but to increase my happiness that he went, and are ashamed to show their face before flowers.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My lack-lustre eyes that are raining down tears look as if they would betray to others the unkindness of my beloved.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The arms that swelled with joy on the nuptial day now look as if they would proclaim his parting to all the world.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The arms that lost their wonted comeliness at the parting of the beloved, are now grown so thin that their very bracelets slip off from them of themselves.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The arms which have lost their wonted comeliness together with the bracelets that they were wearing, proclaim loudly to the world the cruelty of that cruel one.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I chide my arms for growing lean and allowing the bracelets to fall off, as people now reproach him with cruelty.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Wouldst thou obtain glory, O my Heart ? Then run to the cruel one and tell him of the bruit that hath arisen here from the wasting away of my arm.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: As we were embracing each other one day, I but relaxed my arms a little, and the forehead of that artless one grew pale at once !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: But a single breath of wind cut its way between us during our embrace; and the blood fled at once from her large eyes that are full even as the rain-cloud.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Did the eyes grow pale only? They wept also at seeing the pallor of the fair forehead above.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Wouldst thou not think, O my Heart,. and find out and tell me some remedy to cure me of this incurable disease ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bless thee, my Heart! Thou art a fool to grieve at his absence when he hath no love for thee.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What availeth our sitting here and pining away for thinking of him, O my Heart ? He that caused us this grief remembereth us not.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If thou go to him, my Heart, take these eyes also along with thee! For they devour me in their longing to look on him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though he spurneth us in spite of our cleaving unto him, can we give him up as an enemy, my Heart ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When thou lookest on the beloved who is clever in the art of conciliating, my Heart, thou wouldst not even take huff but wouldst rush to his embrace, forgetting all: I fear that now too thy anger is only feigned.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: O my Heart ! Either give up love or give up bashfulness : for, I am unable to support both of them at the same time.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou sighest that he would not return for pity sake, and wouldst go to seek him though he separated deliberately from thee: verily, thou art a simpleton, my Heart !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Whom dost thou seek to join, O my Heart, when thou knowest that the beloved is seated within thy own self ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If we entertain any longer within our hearts the beloved that hath abandoned us, we shall only waste ourselves away yet further.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The door that is bolted with the bolt of modesty will yet yield to the axe of an overpowering love.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Heartless is this thing called Love : for it oppresseth my heart even in the dead of night.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I try indeed to shut my love up within my heart: but like a sneeze it breaketh out of itself without a warning.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I was proud that I was correct and decorous in my behaviour: but alas! love rendeth every veil and showeth itself in public.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The stern self-respect that refuseth to seek the beloved though he hath cruelly deserted, is a thing unknown to the love-sick fair.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: How thou lovest me, O Grief! Thou: wantest me to follow after him who hath deserted me cruelly !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If the beloved but favour us with his love, we at once forget all our reserve.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is the subdued speech of that false-one skilled in many a wily art, that breaketh through all the defences of our womanly decorum.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I wanted to go away in a huff: but I went and embraced him, for I saw that my heart had already joined him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Can they ever think of refusing to be reconciled, whose heart melteth even as fat in the fire ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My eyes have lost their lustre and grown dull, and my fingers have worn away for counting of the days that I have noted on the wall.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What if I forget to-day, my maid ? My beauty hath already left me and my bracelet hath slipped off my arm.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He parted from me longing for conquests: and if I live yet, it is for the longing of his return.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He gave my company up and parted without any regard to my feelings : but yet for the mere thinking of his speedy return my heart swelleth with joy !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Only let my eyes take their fill of the sight of my beloved: pallor will then no more be seen on my wasted arm.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Let my spouse but return home: and then in one day I shall drink the nectar of his presence and bid farewell to this wasting disease.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When the beloved who is dear even as my eyes cometh home, shall I sulk for his long absence ? or shall I embrace him ? or shall I do both ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: May the prince begin the battle at once and triumph! And may I return in the evening and feast at home with my loved one !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To those who count the days and yearn for the return of the beloved who is away, one single day will creep along with the slowness of seven.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail will be my getting back or the meeting or even the hearty embrace, if the heart of my loved one be broken before then ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou mayest try to conceal, my love, but thy eye refuseth to be restrained, and telleth me that there is some strange thought in thy breast.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Ah! More than a woman’s reserve hath my artless one, whose beauty filleth my eyes and whose arms are even as bamboo stems.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as the thread that is seen through the crystal bead, there is a thought that is now passing in her bosom, but which is yet plainly visible.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as the fragrance in the bud that is not yet blown, there is a secret meaning in the half-smile of this artless one.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The cunning with which she concealed her rising thought and left hath a charm to cure the anguish of my heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: He is overkind and sweet to me: I fear there is something in his heart which he is hardly able to conceal : and it forebodeth to me a second departure.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My bracelet hath read the coolness in the heart of my gracious lord even sooner than my own self.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My beloved parted only yesterday : but it is seven days since my form hath lost its freshness !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: She looked at her bracelet and her tender arm and then she looked at her feet : these are the signs that she made to me.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: She telleth me of the pangs of separation and prayeth for permission to accompany me if I go: how she sur-passeth womanhood’s self in delicacy to tell this only with her eyes !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Rapture at the very thought and delight at the mere seeing belong not to wine : they belong only unto love.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When love exceedeth even the measure of a palmyra tree, the desire to sulk can never enter the heart even to the extent of a millet seed.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though he careth not for me and doth only as he pleaseth, my eyes will not rest unless they behold him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I wanted indeed to go away in a huff, my maid: but my heart forgot it and ran after union with the beloved.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even as the eye seeth not the blackness of the pencil when it is being painted, even so I see no blemish in my beloved when he is near.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When he is before me I can see no faults in him : but when I see him not, I can see nothing in him but faults.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Who will jump into a stream knowing that it hath a treacherous undercurrent that will carry him away ? and how should I take to sulking who know that I cannot hold on to it when he is near ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Wine is never unwelcome to the drunkard though it maketh him hang down his head in shame: even so is thy bosom to me, O false one !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even tenderer than a flower is love : and few there be who know its delicacy and deal with it gently.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There were the sulks in her eye when she saw me: but when I approached, she flew to my arms even quicker than I myself to hers.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou seest how his heart serveth his will : then, how is it that thou obeyest not me, O my Heart ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou seest, my Heart, how he neglecteth me: and yet thou consortest with him as if he were thy friend !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou followest him at thy own sweet will and pleasure, my Heart: dost thou also teach me that those who are unfortunate have no friends?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Thou refusest to indulge in a bouderie, my Heart, before showing thy delight in his company : who is going hereafter to take thee as a confidant in such like things?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It feareth lest it should not get him, and when it hath got him, it feareth lest it should lose him: thus there is no end to the pangs that my Heart suffereth.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: What ismy Heart good for ? It is good for nothing else but to devour me when I am musing alone.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Fallen into the company of this foolish Heart that knoweth not to preserve its self-respect by forgetting him, I have myself forgotten my dignity.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: My life of a Heart thinketh it a disgrace to our own Selves if we humiliate the beloved : and so it is always partial to him.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Who will support a man in his grief, if the Heart of his beloved itself refuseth him help ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: When my own heart is not on my side, is it a wonder that strangest care not at all for me ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Embrace him not, my dear, but feign to be angry : let us just see a fun how he is nettled over it.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bouderie is the salt of love: to lengthen it unduly, however, is like adding too much of salt to food.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is like wounding one anew who is already wounded, if thou come away without embracing her whom thou hast left in a pet.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: To come away without conciliating her who is frowning in a pet is like cutting off the roots from under the starving plant.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: The bouderie of the beloved hath an attraction even for men who are spotlessly pure.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If there were no frowns or pets on the part of the beloved, love would miss its fruits and its half-growns.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: There is a pain that belongeth unto bouderie : for one asketh oneself whether reconciliation is near or yet a far way off.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Of what avail is my grieving when there is no loving one nigh to see how much I suffer ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Water is pleasant only in shady groves : and pettishness hath a charm only in one who loveth ardently.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: If my heart still yearneth for her who sootheth me not, it is due to nothing but a foolish longing.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: All that are women devour thee with their eyes, thou gallant! I shall have none of thy embrace.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I was in the sulks: he then sneezed, for he thought that I would bless him saying, Long live my beloved !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if I wear a garland she would go off in a pique saying, Thou wantest to look smart in some damsel’s eyes !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I said to her, I love thee above all: and behold, she frowned at once asking, Above whom? and above whom ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I told her, We shall never part in this life: alack, her eyes at once filled with tears !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I said to her, I called thee to mind when away: and she that was about to clasp me to her arms went off in a pet saying, Thou hadst forgotten me then !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I sneezed and she blessed : but then she recalled her blessing and asked with tear-filled eyes, Who thought on thee now, that thou sneezedest ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: I repressed my sneeze: and then also she wept saying, Thou wantest to conceal from me that some of thy friends are thinking on thee !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if I exhaust all my arts to soothe her, she will only frown harder saying, Thou hast practised well at others’ bouderies !
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if I look in rapture on her own charms; she will chide saying, To whose limbs now art thou comparing mine ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even if he is free from faults, it is only bouderie that giveth me a taste of his conciliatory grace.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Though the tenderness of the beloved hath to wait a little, there is a charm in the pinprick that we feel in being pettish.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Is there a higher heaven than bouderie, provided that the beloved is one with us, even as the water with the land whereon it floweth ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: In my very quarrel with my beloved lieth the engine that stormeth the defences of my heart.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Even when one is free from faults there is a delight when the arms of the beloved are withdrawn from one’s clasp.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Sweeter is digestion than the meal : even so is the lovers’ quarrel sweeter than the embrace.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: It is the one who yieldeth first who is the winner in lovers’ quarrels : thou canst see it indeed at the hour of reconciliation.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Verily, will she give some piquancy to the delights of our embrace by just feigning a quarrel for some time ?
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Oh, let me enjoy her frowning and her pouting a little more! Only let night prolong her reign at my prayer.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar

text: Bouderie is the charm of love: and the charm of that again is the sweet embrace at its close.
author: V. V. S. Aiyar
work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar
